places.name: Bogmother

why.founding: An ancient sacred site south-west of Stormhold, ruined for centuries and never abandoned, holding relics venerable enough that nobody moved them.
why.siteAdvantages: At the far end of a stone causeway from Stormhold — the causeway exists because the site does, not the other way round.
why.occupantsMotive: A caretaker few keep it swept and the relics in place; the city funds them because being seen not to would be intolerable.
why.pressures: Crocodiles have moved inside the town threshold and the caretakers have decided not to remove them.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be robbed within a season if the caretakers left, and the city would blame itself for centuries.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: a landmark for its whole district; a village within 1 km tends it
hardConstraints: at the end of a stone causeway

notableNpcSlots: the eldest caretaker, who feeds the crocodiles

vibe.silhouette: Terraced stone half-sunk in bog, swept clean above the waterline and green below it, with wide flooded courts.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, black water, the caretakers' white cloth, and green to the exact height of the flood.
vibe.materials: Ancient Argonian terrace stone; the caretakers add nothing but brooms, cloth and offerings.
vibe.signatureFeature: The relics, still in place in an open chamber, in a ruin with no door.
vibe.condition: Ruined for centuries and immaculately maintained as a ruin — a distinction the caretakers will explain.
vibe.mood: Holy, patient, quietly dangerous at ankle height.
vibe.approach: The causeway runs at it straight over open bog; you see the terraces for the last four hundred metres.
vibe.senses: Brooms; water displaced by something large; no birds inside the walls.

provisions: the sacred ruin at the causeway's end

places.name: Branchmont

why.founding: An Archein saltrice estate south-west of Thorn whose owners embezzled themselves out of existence, leaving a village and no landlord.
why.siteAdvantages: The best saltrice ground outside Thorn's own fields, level and floodable on demand.
why.occupantsMotive: The villagers work it as their own; three separate claimants say otherwise, and one of them is Dunmer.
why.pressures: The dispute is in Thorn's title court and has been for eleven years, which suits the villagers perfectly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be settled violently the first time a claimant arrived with hands rather than papers.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: controls a crossing or a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: holds the crossing its neighbours must use
hardConstraints: an estate house with no occupant

occupants: D1 villagers working as their own masters
D2 hired watch on the boundary
notableNpcSlots: the village's chosen speaker
the Dunmer claimant's factor, who visits and is fed

vibe.silhouette: A shuttered estate house standing empty in the middle of fields that are visibly being worked by somebody.
vibe.palette: Saltrice silver-green, estate-house white going grey, and new thatch on the old worker rows.
vibe.materials: Archein estate masonry, unoccupied; the worker rows have been re-roofed and extended in reed.
vibe.signatureFeature: The house: swept, shuttered, unlived-in, and the whole village's most carefully maintained building.
vibe.condition: Fields excellent, rows improved, house frozen.
vibe.approach: The white house shows across flat fields for a kilometre and reads, correctly, as the wrong thing in the picture.
vibe.senses: Water in the sluices; work songs; the shutters of an empty house.

places.name: Channel Cross

why.founding: Where two navigable channels cross, everything stops, so a village stands on the crossing itself.
why.siteAdvantages: The junction of the trunk channel and the Bogmother feeder — every boat in the district passes through it.
why.occupantsMotive: It lives on pilotage: the channels braid and only local people know which arm is open this season.
why.pressures: The pilots have begun charging by the season rather than the trip, which the boat crews call a toll.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be irrelevant if anyone ever dredged and marked the braids properly.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: strung along a waterway, linear not radial
preferences: a pilot's platform with sightlines up both channels

occupants: D2 crews waiting on a pilot
notableNpcSlots: the senior pilot who keeps the braid map in her head

vibe.silhouette: A tall pilot's platform at the middle of a water crossroads, with the village built outward from it in four arms.
vibe.palette: Black water in four directions, reed roofs, and one raised platform with a lamp on it.
vibe.materials: Stilt construction with one deliberately over-tall structure — the only vertical in the district.
vibe.signatureFeature: The pilot platform: high enough to see up all four channels, which is the whole reason the village exists.
vibe.condition: Sound; the platform is the best-maintained thing for kilometres.
vibe.approach: The platform lamp is visible up all four channels at night, which is the province's cue language working properly.
vibe.senses: Water from four directions; a horn used to call pilots; poles.

places.name: Crystalgate

why.founding: Stormhold's crystal has to be cut, graded and sold somewhere that is not the city, because the city taxes what passes its gates.
why.siteAdvantages: On the road between the diggings and the Tear road, at the first spring outside Stormhold's jurisdiction.
why.occupantsMotive: The cutting houses are guild-like and hereditary; the town exists entirely downstream of one skill.
why.pressures: The vicecanons want the cutting inside the walls and have tried tariffs twice.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse into a road village the day the Silyanorn seams ran out — which the diggers say is a generation away.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: at its resource and its haul route
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: paired with a diggings, salt pans, clay pit or fishery

notableNpcSlots: the grand grader
the cutter who is going blind

vibe.silhouette: A town of long low sheds all facing the same way, with north-facing window slots and a single tall grading hall.
vibe.palette: Blue-green crystal dust on everything, shed-timber grey, and one whitewashed hall.
vibe.materials: Mud-brick and timber sheds built to a single plan, which no other Argonian town is.
vibe.signatureFeature: The uniform orientation: every shed faces north for the light, so the whole town points the same way.
vibe.condition: Purpose-built, well kept, monotonous by local standards.
vibe.approach: The town reads as a grid of parallel roofs from the road above — the only regular plan in the north.
vibe.senses: Continuous small chinking; water wheels; someone calling grades aloud.

places.name: The Anachronistic Library
sources: docs/quests/20-world-provisions.md §12b (Conclave of Baal and the Vaults of Gemin)

why.founding: A collection inside an Ayleid tomb that contains books written long after the tomb was sealed, and continues to acquire them.
why.siteAdvantages: The deepest dry chamber of the fenlord's complex — the only room in the north where paper survives.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing tends it and it is nonetheless catalogued, in a hand that changes every few centuries.
why.pressures: The Conclave of Baal at Stormhold reads the Elder Scrolls with an ancient tablet, and the tablet's provenance leads here.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the single most valuable room in the province if anyone could carry anything out of it.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in a ruin, or in a northern city
hardConstraints: a dry chamber inside a sealed complex

vibe.silhouette: A dry vaulted room of shelves, lit blue, with books on them from every century including this one.
vibe.palette: Welkynd blue on white stone, leather, and the warm brown of paper that should not exist.
vibe.materials: Ayleid shelving cut from the wall itself; the books are the only non-Ayleid objects in the complex.
vibe.signatureFeature: The catalogue: continuously maintained, in a series of hands, the most recent entry very recent.
vibe.condition: Bone dry, in a building standing in a fen. That is not an accident.
vibe.approach: You reach it last, through the flooded levels, which is why almost nobody has.
vibe.senses: Absolutely nothing — the one place in the province with no water sound at all.

why.founding: A Barsaebic Ayleid fenlord's tomb, undead-guarded, whose library has never stopped attracting volumes.
why.siteAdvantages: Sunk in fen on the least accessible ground within a day of Stormhold — the fenlord chose privacy.
why.occupantsMotive: The dead here still hold the office they held; nothing living has taken the place from them.
why.pressures: Books keep arriving. Nobody can say how, and the Conclave at Stormhold has views it will not share.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a Synod prize the day anyone proved the collection could be moved.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near a Barsaebic compound

vibe.silhouette: White Ayleid stonework rising out of black fen water, half of it below the surface, all of it lit from within.
vibe.palette: Bone white, welkynd blue, black water.
vibe.materials: Barsaebic Ayleid masonry and welkynd lighting, entirely intact — the best-preserved Ayleid work in the province.
vibe.signatureFeature: The lit windows: the tomb is illuminated inside, continuously, and has been for four thousand years.
vibe.condition: Structurally perfect and completely submerged at the lowest level.
vibe.approach: The blue light on the water is visible at night for six hundred metres — the north's most striking approach.
vibe.senses: Water against stone; a hum from the welkynd stones; footsteps that are not yours, in step.

places.name: Greylight

why.founding: A Hist stands here, so a village does; the north's Hist are fewer and further apart than the interior's, which makes each one political.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm hummock in the Shadowfen channels, the only one within half a day.
why.occupantsMotive: The village mediates for four water-villages that have no tree of their own, which gives it standing it did not seek.
why.pressures: Stormhold wants the tree's sanction for things the tree has no opinion about, and sends gifts about it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not move; a Hist village does not. But its politics could change in a season.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: channel bank or spring, always with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage
hardConstraints: a living Hist on firm ground

notableNpcSlots: the naheesh who mediates for four villages
the minder who refuses Stormhold's gifts

vibe.silhouette: A pale crown standing over the channel canopy with four landing stages around the hummock beneath it, one per village.
vibe.palette: Hist grey-white, channel black, four different mooring-post carvings.
vibe.materials: Mud, wattle and reed; the four stages are each built in the visiting village's own style.
vibe.signatureFeature: The four stages: you can tell which villages are speaking to Greylight by which stages are maintained.
vibe.condition: Village rebuilt on the usual cycle; the stages vary wildly in condition.
vibe.mood: Diplomatic, patient, slightly weary of being needed.
vibe.approach: The crown reads over the canopy from the channels at a kilometre — the north's clearest natural landmark.
vibe.senses: Poles arriving; the uxith; four dialects on one hummock.

places.name: The Hatching Pools

why.founding: The regional hatchery: the one institution a depopulating province cannot let lapse, rebuilt after the Dominion massacre and again after Umbriel.
why.siteAdvantages: Warm spring-fed shallows at a constant temperature, screened on every side — the pools were found, not made.
why.occupantsMotive: The Keepers of the Shell stay because the alternative is that a generation is not born; canon shows them dying rather than leaving.
why.pressures: It has been attacked twice in living memory and is defended accordingly; outsiders are not welcome and are not always refused.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the single greatest loss the north could suffer, which is why it is the most defended non-city site in the province.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: warm still water, no flood risk
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: serves 4-8 villages; approaches watched
preferences: a keepers' compound above the pools

notableNpcSlots: the warden-mother
the tender who survived the massacre as an egg

vibe.silhouette: A stockade of stakes around a bowl of steaming pale-green pools, with low sheds on the rim and nothing tall anywhere.
vibe.palette: Pool jade-green, steam white, stockade black, and the pale of shell.
vibe.materials: Stockade pikes and mud-and-reed sheds; the pools themselves are untouched ground.
vibe.signatureFeature: The counting stones on the rim: one stone per clutch, going back further than the current stockade.
vibe.condition: Rebuilt twice within memory, and everything shows which rebuild it belongs to.
vibe.mood: Reverent, guarded, warm in the literal sense — the only warm place in the marsh.
vibe.approach: You are stopped a long way out. The reveal is a warden, not a view.
vibe.senses: Water at blood heat; steam; a constant low chorus that is not frogs.

places.name: Hixinoag
sources: uesp:Lore:Black Marsh (most villages do not stay put)
world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md §5 (G3.3: genuinely drifting villages, hand-authored; Hixinoag is the canon-named one of two)

why.founding: The province's one genuinely drifting village: a jumble of huts half-sunk in mud that moves with the flood cycle along the northern caravan route.
why.siteAdvantages: It occupies two or three fixed moorings in turn, chosen because each is good at a different water level.
why.occupantsMotive: The people move because moving is cheaper than repairing, and because being hard to find has been good for them.
why.pressures: Caravans that miss the mooring lose a day; the village charges accordingly and is not sorry.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would settle permanently only if one mooring became good in every season, which the hydrology forbids.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: its moorings are on a caravan or boat route
hardConstraints: two or three fixed moorings on one route
preferences: an empty mooring readable as a place

occupants: D1 village households wherever it currently is
notableNpcSlots: the mooring-caller who decides when to move

vibe.silhouette: Forty huts jammed together at whatever angle the mud allowed, half-sunk, with the mooring posts of the last site still standing empty two hours away.
vibe.palette: Mud brown on mud brown, with roof thatch the only colour and a great deal of it askew.
vibe.materials: Mud-and-reed huts built to be abandoned; nothing is fixed to anything.
vibe.signatureFeature: The empty mooring: the posts, the flattened ground, the hearth rings — a POI in its own right when the village is elsewhere.
vibe.condition: Deliberately shoddy; anything well built would be a mistake.
vibe.mood: Cheerful, mercenary, impossible to pin down.
vibe.approach: You are told where it was. Finding it is the content.
vibe.senses: Mud sucking; huts settling audibly; a great deal of talking.

places.name: Mazzatun

why.founding: The Xit-Xaht built in stone after the Duskfall said not to, under the direction of a Hist they had enslaved with sap.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep in the north-east swamp on ground nobody else contests, screened by rootland and reputation together.
why.occupantsMotive: Tsono-Xuhil's convalescent sleep is canon-indefinite; three and a half centuries on the Amber Plasm seep has resumed and the building has restarted.
why.pressures: The neighbours say only 'the Hist is crazy' and stay away — which is the only reason the building has never been stopped.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a province-wide emergency the day another tribe accepted the Xit-Xaht's invitation to help.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: stone source and a haul water
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: raids its neighbours for labour

notableNpcSlots: the shaper who directs the building
a labourer who has begun to remember

vibe.silhouette: A city being built out of stone in a province that stopped: scaffolds, half-cut blocks, and a great tree at the centre with tubes in it.
vibe.palette: Wet green-black stone, amber sap, and the sick pale of the workers.
vibe.materials: Cut stone, cane scaffolding, and sap conduits of hollowed root — an architecture nobody else in Argonia would make.
vibe.signatureFeature: The conduits: amber tubes running from the Hist into the works, feeding the labour rather than the tree.
vibe.condition: Under construction, three and a half centuries late, and visibly resumed within the last decade.
vibe.approach: The sound of stone being cut carries a long way through swamp, and it is the only such sound in the province.
vibe.senses: Chisels; a wet dripping from the conduits; workers who do not talk.

provisions: the enslaved Hist and the stone heresy

places.name: Tsono-Xuhil

why.founding: A Hist coerced with sap into directing a city's construction, and left in a convalescent sleep that canon never ends.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands where it always stood; the city was built around it, not the other way round.
why.occupantsMotive: The Xit-Xaht tend it in the way a farmer tends a crop, and describe that as devotion.
why.pressures: The seep has resumed, slowly, which either means it is healing or that it is dreaming again.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would change everything in the north if it woke — and there is a mnemic egg here that might tell you which it is doing.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: beside a bereaved or sap-touched village

occupants: nothing else will come near it

vibe.silhouette: A vast crown, greyer than a Hist should be, with amber running down its bark in fixed channels.
vibe.palette: Sick grey bark, amber, and a canopy that is thinner than the trees around it.
vibe.materials: The tree, and the tubes. Nothing else here is architecture.
vibe.signatureFeature: The amber egg cradled in the first fork — a memory that has been put somewhere for safekeeping.
vibe.condition: Alive, harmed, and possibly recovering.
vibe.mood: Grievous. It is the single saddest object in the north.
vibe.approach: The crown shows above the canopy from a kilometre — a Hist landmark that means the opposite of what a Hist landmark means.
vibe.senses: Dripping sap; a silence in the canopy where birdsong should be.

places.name: Murkwater

why.founding: A Shadowfen village with a Shadowscale association, liberated by them in 2E 582 and quietly proud of it ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: A Hist on a firm hummock in the channel network, with water approaches on every side.
why.occupantsMotive: It stays because the Hist is here; it keeps its Shadowscale connection because the connection has twice saved it.
why.pressures: The Archon sanctuary closed in 4E 187, so the surviving ku-vastei who lives here is the last of an institution.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a pilgrimage site the day the Shadowscales were publicly ended, and the village would hate that.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: channel bank or spring, always with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage
preferences: a retired ku-vastei's house set apart

occupants: one very strong D4 retired ku-vastei
notableNpcSlots: the retired ku-vastei
the naheesh who was a child in 2E 582

vibe.silhouette: A Hist crown over reed roofs on a hummock, with one house standing apart on its own small island.
vibe.palette: Hist grey-white, reed gold, black channel water, and a single black door on the separate house.
vibe.materials: Standard Argonian mud, wattle and reed; the separate house is identical except that it has a door.
vibe.signatureFeature: The house apart: everyone knows who lives there and nobody points.
vibe.condition: Well kept, rebuilt on the usual cycle, older at the centre.
vibe.approach: By boat the crown appears first; the separate house is the last thing you notice and the thing you remember.
vibe.senses: Poles in water; the uxith; a village that lowers its voice near one house.

places.name: The Tempering Ground

why.founding: Children born under the Shadow were given up and made into something else, and the making happened on set ground, away from the village.
why.siteAdvantages: A screened hollow an hour from Murkwater — close enough to deliver a child to, far enough that nobody heard.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody keeps it now. The Archon sanctuary closed in 4E 187 and the ground has had no purpose since.
why.pressures: The equipment is still here, and the ku-vastei in the village has never come back to remove it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be destroyed the day someone decided the institution should not be reconstituted — and someone will try.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near a hatchery and a major city, deliberately unremarkable
hardConstraints: screened from a village, within an hour of it
preferences: a delivery stone at the entrance

occupants: D3 that has moved into the course

vibe.silhouette: A hollow with a course still laid out in it — beams, ropes, pits — everything rotted and everything still in position.
vibe.palette: Rotted rope grey, green overgrowth, and one pale stone at the entrance.
vibe.materials: Timber, rope and pits; the only stone is the delivery stone.
vibe.signatureFeature: The delivery stone: flat, waist-high, at the entrance, worn smooth in one place.
vibe.condition: Abandoned fourteen years, rotting fast, entirely undisturbed.
vibe.mood: Cold, purposeful, unbearable when you understand the stone.
vibe.approach: There is no path any more; you are told where it is or you never find it.
vibe.senses: Rope creaking with nothing on it; birds; the hollow's odd flat acoustic.

places.name: Reedmoor

why.founding: Shadowfen's channels have no dry ground worth building on, so the villages stand on legs over the water.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide slow reach with a firm bed for piling — the bed matters more than the bank here.
why.occupantsMotive: It fishes, cuts reed and poles cargo for the trunk route; three trades, none of which need land.
why.pressures: The bed is silting and the piles are being driven shorter each rebuild, which the elders discuss constantly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move two hundred metres downstream, entire, in the way this province's villages always have.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: strung along a waterway, linear not radial

occupants: D2 in the water at night
notableNpcSlots: the pile-driver, an office as much as a job

vibe.silhouette: Forty reed houses standing on legs over open water, with a single broad platform at the centre and boats racked beneath everything.
vibe.palette: Reed gold above, black water below, and the pale of new-cut piles.
vibe.materials: Stilt shells and elevated walkways; nothing touches the ground and there is no ground to touch.
vibe.signatureFeature: The pile forest below: two centuries of abandoned piles still standing under the village, a submerged history.
vibe.condition: Continuously rebuilt; the newest houses are at the downstream end.
vibe.mood: Buoyant, noisy, entirely at ease with water.
vibe.approach: The village reads as a line of roofs floating on nothing from four hundred metres of open channel.
vibe.senses: Water under floors; poles; children in the water constantly.

places.name: Riverwalk

why.founding: The northern trunk's mid-point: a village strung along a channel because the channel is the street.
why.siteAdvantages: Two hours' poling from either end of the day's run — the trunk route's natural halt.
why.occupantsMotive: It lives on the ferry stage, the toll and feeding boat crews; nothing here is grown.
why.pressures: Alten Corimont's captain and Thorn's field-owners both think the toll should be theirs.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be bypassed if a deeper channel opened south, and the villagers watch the silt for exactly that.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: crosses water rather than sitting beside it
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: often the only dry route through its stretch
hardConstraints: a navigable channel as the main street
preferences: a toll post at the narrow

notableNpcSlots: the toll-holder
the stage-mistress

vibe.silhouette: A single boardwalk a kilometre long with houses on both sides of it, and no land under any of them.
vibe.palette: Silver weathered plank, black water, reed roofs in a continuous run.
vibe.materials: Elevated walkway construction throughout: piles, planks, stilt shells and lashed handrails.
vibe.signatureFeature: The length: the village is one street and no cross-streets, so you meet everyone in it.
vibe.condition: Constantly re-planked; the boards are all different ages and you can read the village's history by walking it.
vibe.approach: By boat you enter the village at one end and pole its whole length — the arrival is a procession.
vibe.senses: Boards underfoot for a kilometre; poles; talk from directly above the water.

places.name: Saltmarch

why.founding: A field village of Argonians and Dunmer working the same crop, founded when the estates broke up and the labour stayed.
why.siteAdvantages: In the middle of the terraces, on the one rise that never floods, equidistant from four banks.
why.occupantsMotive: They farm together and marry separately, which is the arrangement and has been for three generations.
why.pressures: Thorn's title court could dissolve their common holding with one ruling and they know it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would split cleanly in two along a line everyone can already see, if it ever came to that.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in a city's agricultural hinterland
hardConstraints: a rise inside the terrace system
preferences: two shrine types in one village

occupants: D1 mixed Argonian and Dunmer households
notableNpcSlots: the field-speaker
the Dunmer elder who keeps the other calendar

vibe.silhouette: Round Argonian houses and square lacquered Dunmer ones alternating along one street, with a single shared threshing floor.
vibe.palette: Thatch gold, lacquer red, saltrice silver on every horizon.
vibe.materials: Two unblended architectures interleaved house by house — the two-culture rule made into a street.
vibe.signatureFeature: The shared threshing floor with two shrine niches on opposite walls, both used.
vibe.condition: Prosperous and continuously extended in both styles.
vibe.mood: Practical, mixed, quietly proud of being unusual.
vibe.approach: The alternating roof shapes read from the terrace banks and are unlike anything else in the province.
vibe.senses: Threshing; two languages; two kinds of cooking at once.

places.name: The Silyanorn Diggings

why.founding: Stormhold's crystal trade comes out of a Barsaebic Ayleid undercity that the city has been quarrying for centuries.
why.siteAdvantages: The ravine walls below the city expose the Ayleid galleries directly — the diggings are the ruin, entered sideways.
why.occupantsMotive: The vicecanons license the diggings because the crystal pays for the border offices; the diggers dig because the Owing says so.
why.pressures: Every season takes more of an Ayleid structure that the Synod would pay handsomely to study intact.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be closed by any authority that valued the ruin above the revenue, which is no authority the north has.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: drainage problems are the mine's whole story
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: feeds a northern city's crystal trade
hardConstraints: exposed Ayleid galleries in a ravine wall

notableNpcSlots: the digging-master
the digger who has found a room nobody has reported

vibe.silhouette: Timber hoists running down a ravine wall into square white doorways that are obviously not natural.
vibe.palette: Ayleid bone-white, welkynd blue in the depths, ravine black, timber grey.
vibe.materials: Ayleid ashlar galleries with modern timber shoring driven straight through the carving.
vibe.signatureFeature: The shoring: props hammered into four-thousand-year-old reliefs, which nobody here even sees any more.
vibe.condition: The Ayleid work is perfect; everything added to it is failing.
vibe.approach: From the city terraces above you look straight down into the gallery mouths — a vertical reveal.
vibe.senses: Hoists; picks on stone; a welkynd hum under the noise.

places.name: Stillrise Village

why.founding: A village that took a Daedric bargain to survive the Knahaten Flu and has been technically dead ever since, sustained by a soul-gem array.
why.siteAdvantages: West of Stormhold on ground the Flu emptied around them — they are the only thing left on it.
why.occupantsMotive: They maintain the illusions because the alternative is to stop; three and a half centuries of infighting has settled nothing.
why.pressures: The array was preserved rather than destroyed in 2E 582, so the argument that started then is still running, with the same participants.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end the day someone broke the array — and half the village would thank them.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: shunned by its neighbours, who nevertheless maintain the markers
hardConstraints: a village that appears normal at distance
preferences: an argument that is visibly three centuries old

occupants: one D4 who maintains the array
notableNpcSlots: the array-keeper
the villager who wants it broken

vibe.silhouette: An ordinary village that stops being ordinary at about thirty metres, when the illusion stops covering the detail.
vibe.palette: Warm ochre and thatch at distance; bone, cobweb and grey-green at close range.
vibe.materials: Ordinary mud-and-reed houses, maintained by hands that do not need to eat, so the thatch is perfect and unrepaired for centuries.
vibe.signatureFeature: The array itself, in the meeting house: soul gems in a frame, humming, the whole village's life support.
vibe.condition: Unchanged since 2E 582 in every particular, which is itself the horror.
vibe.approach: It looks like a normal village from the path — the reveal is entirely in the approach, and it is a slow one.
vibe.senses: Voices that are slightly too dry; the array's hum; no cooking smells at all.

places.name: Stormhold

why.founding: Built on ravine-severed mounds above a waterfall, over a Barsaebic Ayleid crystal undercity the city has never stopped mining.
why.siteAdvantages: The head of navigation on the northern river: everything from Morrowind stops here, and the ravines make each mound its own defensible quarter.
why.occupantsMotive: The vicecanons — plural, and rivals — run the state's only working border offices because the river trade pays for offices.
why.pressures: The Knahaten Flu began here, and the city has never been allowed to forget it; the Silyanorn tunnels below are worked by people with no other option.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose its purpose if the Morrowind trade failed, and its shape if the waterfall ever cut back past the first mound.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: astride a navigable river above the falls
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the northern hinge: Tenmar Wall east, Bogmother south-west, the Morrowind road north
preferences: an undercity entrance inside the walls

occupants: D1 city population (Argonian majority, 22% Dunmer per module 92)
one very strong D3 tunnel overseer
notableNpcSlots: the two rival vicecanons
the Conclave of Baal's reader
the Collections alcove-keeper
the tunnel overseer

vibe.silhouette: Three terraced mounds stepping above a white waterfall, linked by bridges, with black ravine slots between them.
vibe.palette: Wet grey terrace stone, white water, dark ravine, and crystal-blue points in the undercity mouths at night.
vibe.materials: Argonian terrace construction over Barsaebic Ayleid foundations, with Dunmer-frontier timber balconies on the trade quarter.
vibe.signatureFeature: The undercity mouths: three worked openings in the ravine walls, lit blue, with hoists running into them.
vibe.condition: Prosperous on the top terraces, worked-out and propped below the waterline of the ravines.
vibe.mood: Layered, factional, damp — a city where every quarter looks down on another literally.
vibe.approach: By river you come up to the falls and the city is stacked above you; by road you arrive at the top and look down into it.
vibe.senses: Waterfall constantly under everything; hoists; three languages; a bell per mound.

provisions: the Conclave of Baal, who locate Murkwood by reading the Elder Scrolls with an ancient tablet

places.complexityJustification: A major city on ravine-severed mounds with an undercity: three district clusters, bridges and a vertical layer. Placement stays Morrowind-level, but the mound/bridge/undercity structure justifies the budget.

places.name: The Bogmother Causeway

why.founding: Stormhold built a stone causeway to Bogmother because the pilgrimage could not wait on the season.
why.siteAdvantages: The shortest line of shallow bog between the city's south gate and the sacred ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The city maintains it as a civic duty; the maintenance gang is a hereditary office with a bad reputation.
why.pressures: It is stone, which post-Duskfall is a moral compromise — and it is the only reason the compromise is tolerated.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced with timber if it ever failed completely, which the caretakers would prefer and the city would not.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: links two named places directly
hardConstraints: shallow bog between two fixed points

occupants: D2 pilgrims and the maintenance gang
D3 in the bog either side after dark

vibe.silhouette: A raised stone road three paces wide running dead straight over open bog with no rail of any kind.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, brown bog, and a very large amount of sky for this province.
vibe.materials: Cut stone slabs on a rubble core — the largest single piece of stone construction the north has built since the Duskfall.
vibe.signatureFeature: The subsidence: whole sections tilt, so the causeway reads as a line of slightly wrong angles.
vibe.condition: Continuously repaired and continuously sinking.
vibe.approach: It goes flat to the horizon out of the city's south gate, which is the only straight line for kilometres.
vibe.senses: Feet on stone — an unfamiliar sound here; bog gas; wind with nothing to break it.

why.founding: The Tear road is one of the province's two canon exit roads, and a road to Morrowind needs a last stage on the Argonian side.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the road leaves the marsh for the pass — the last place with fodder, water and level ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The stage is run by a family who take payment in both coin and salt and prefer salt.
why.pressures: Dunmer caravans and Argonian porters use the same yard and keep to opposite sides of it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a border town if the traffic doubled, and everyone here can name the year they think that will happen.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: day-travel spacing; something named within 300 m of the road
hardConstraints: last level ground before the pass

vibe.silhouette: Two walled yards sharing one gate and one well, with a fodder barn between them like a partition.
vibe.palette: Dust, Velothi red on one side of the yard, Argonian ochre on the other, and a grey barn between.
vibe.materials: Mud-brick and reed, with a Dunmer-built stone well the caravans paid for and the family did not want.
vibe.signatureFeature: The barn as a wall: it was built across the yard, deliberately, and everyone pretends it was for the fodder.
vibe.condition: Busy, worn, well provisioned.
vibe.approach: The road climbs and the yards appear in the last hollow before the pass.
vibe.senses: Guar and pack-beasts of two kinds; two languages; a well windlass.

why.founding: A Daedric site beside the northern road hinge, and a former Dunmer slave camp — two kinds of atrocity on one piece of ground.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside the junction where the roads from Helstrom, Stormhold and Alten Corimont meet, which is why everyone knows it and nobody enters it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. The marker posts around it are maintained, which is the loudest thing about the place.
why.pressures: The town next door lives off the junction and pretends the ruin is scenery.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would draw a cult within a year if the markers ever stopped being renewed.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: deliberately avoided by every route

vibe.silhouette: A black stone shrine in a clearing, ringed at forty metres by white-painted posts that are obviously new.
vibe.palette: Black stone, white posts, and grass that is a different green inside the ring.
vibe.materials: Daedric black basalt; the slave-camp footings beside it are ordinary Dunmer-cut stone, which is somehow worse.
vibe.signatureFeature: The marker ring: repainted annually by a town that will not say who does it.
vibe.condition: Intact. Nothing here has fallen down, which for a two-thousand-year-old ruin is the tell.
vibe.approach: You can see it from the junction — it is deliberately not hidden, and that is the point.
vibe.senses: Nothing inside the ring; ordinary marsh noise outside it, which makes the contrast.

places.name: Tenmar Wall

why.founding: A town grew at the junction canon names as a neighbour of Helstrom, Stormhold and Alten Corimont at once — the only three-way road hinge in the north.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground where three approaches converge, with water enough for a market and none of the flooding of the roads either side.
why.occupantsMotive: It exists to take a cut of everything passing between the interior, the border city and the smugglers' port.
why.pressures: It is prosperous, indefensible, and next door to a Daedric ruin it refuses to discuss.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be fought over the moment any of the three roads mattered militarily.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: a junction of navigable waters, or a road crossing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the hinge of a district; several villages depend on it
hardConstraints: a three-way road junction on firm ground

notableNpcSlots: the market-warden who allocates pitches by road of origin

vibe.silhouette: A square town with three gates and no fourth wall, and a market square with the pitches laid out in three wedges.
vibe.palette: Dust ochre, awning colours from three different regions, and the black ruin visible past the eastern gate.
vibe.materials: Mud-brick and reed, with an interior-style uxith on the west side and Stormhold terrace stone at the north gate.
vibe.signatureFeature: The three wedges: goods from each road are sold in their own third of the square, and mixing them is a fine.
vibe.condition: Well kept, expanding, entirely unfortified.
vibe.mood: Cosmopolitan by northern standards, superstitious, sharp.
vibe.approach: All three roads run at it and the market noise carries further than the roofs do.
vibe.senses: Three dialects; guar and porters; a market bell at each of three gates.

places.name: The Ash Holding

why.founding: Dres families displaced by the Red Year settled the Argonian side of the pass, on land that was cheap because it had been theirs by force before.
why.siteAdvantages: Upland grazing and a spring, close enough to the pass to leave quickly if they ever have to.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay because Morrowind has nothing left for them; they hold themselves apart because the alternative is admitting that.
why.pressures: Every Argonian household within a day of them is descended from someone this family's ancestors owned.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would leave in a generation if the border ever hardened, and would take the herds.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the Tear road and the Morrowind frontier
preferences: an ancestor tomb cut into rock

notableNpcSlots: the house-mother
the Argonian herder whose grandmother's name is in their ledger

vibe.silhouette: A walled compound with a low tower and a tomb door cut into the rock behind it, on bare upland grazing.
vibe.palette: Ash grey render, red lacquer trim, black tomb door, brown grazing.
vibe.materials: Velothi construction in stone and timber — the only unblended Dunmer architecture in the province outside Thorn's quarter.
vibe.signatureFeature: The tomb door: a Dunmer ancestor tomb cut into Argonian rock, sealed and swept.
vibe.condition: Solid, defensive, unweathered because they render it every year.
vibe.mood: Proud, cold, unwelcome and aware of it.
vibe.approach: The tower shows on the skyline from the road — a foreign silhouette, deliberately.
vibe.senses: Guar; a wind chime of a kind not made here; nothing Argonian at all.

why.founding: The Bogmother causeway ends at a channel too deep to bridge in stone, so the last two hundred metres are a ferry.
why.siteAdvantages: The channel's narrowest point, where the causeway was built up to and then stopped.
why.occupantsMotive: The ferry family are the causeway gang's cousins and the arrangement is inherited and resented.
why.pressures: Pilgrims arriving at dusk find the ferry on the far side more often than chance would explain.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced by a span the day Stormhold decided to spend the money, which it never has.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: across water too deep or wide to ford
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: a mandatory node in the route graph; has a paired stage
hardConstraints: a deep channel interrupting a causeway
preferences: a stone slipway at each end

vibe.silhouette: A stone causeway that simply stops at the water, with a slipway, a bell post and a raft usually on the wrong side.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, black water, and a rope that disappears into it.
vibe.materials: Cut stone slipway and a tarred plank ferry — a Stormhold-built approach and a village-built crossing.
vibe.signatureFeature: The stop: the causeway's last slab is cut square, as if the builders expected to continue.
vibe.condition: Slipway sound, ferry patched, bell rope frayed.
vibe.approach: You walk a kilometre of straight stone and it ends at water with a bell.
vibe.senses: The bell, ringing for a long time; water; the ferry starting from the far bank.

places.name: The North Bone Stage

why.founding: Argonians die in Morrowind — in Tear's yards, in the Owings, on the road — and their bones come back down the pass.
why.siteAdvantages: The first stage on the Argonian side of the pass, because the carry from Tear is the longest in the world and the first rest matters most.
why.occupantsMotive: The keepers meet carriers at the border post and take custody there, which was negotiated and is honoured.
why.pressures: More bones come down the pass each year, and nobody in Thorn will say publicly why.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a scandal if the border post ever refused a carrier, which it has not yet done.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a walked or poled route
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: between a carceral site and the interior

notableNpcSlots: the keeper who counts what comes down the pass

vibe.silhouette: A house and a bone house with a stone between them, on the first flat ground below the pass.
vibe.palette: Limewash white on the bone house, thatch on the other, and the pass grey above both.
vibe.materials: Mud and reed, with the bone house limewashed and a single dressed receiving stone.
vibe.signatureFeature: The count board inside: how many came down the pass, by year, and the line is going the wrong way.
vibe.condition: Well kept; the limewash is renewed monthly, as the rite requires.
vibe.approach: It is the first roof you see coming down off the pass, and there are two of them with a gap.
vibe.senses: Wind off the pass; low talk; the specific sound of a bundle being set down carefully.

places.name: The Borrowed Tomb

why.founding: A Dunmer wayside tomb on the Tear road, emptied by its own family when they left, and lived in since by a road family with nowhere else.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry, stone, roofed and beside the road — the only free shelter on a three-hour stretch.
why.occupantsMotive: They live in the antechamber and have never opened the inner door, which they mention to every guest.
why.pressures: Passing Dunmer find it obscene; passing Argonians find the scruple about the inner door unnecessary.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be vacated instantly and apologetically if any Dres heir arrived.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: inside any ruin type
hardConstraints: an emptied Velothi tomb on a road

occupants: nothing behind the inner door, they hope

vibe.silhouette: A stone tomb doorway beside the road with washing hung across it and a cooking fire in the antechamber.
vibe.palette: Grey Velothi stone, domestic colour spilling out of it, road dust.
vibe.materials: Velothi tomb masonry with a reed lean-to added at the door — the two-culture rule as an accident of poverty.
vibe.signatureFeature: The inner door: swept clean, never opened, with a bowl left in front of it every evening.
vibe.condition: Structurally excellent and domestically improvised.
vibe.approach: It is a tomb door with laundry on it, visible from the road, and takes a moment to parse.
vibe.senses: Cooking in a stone chamber, with the echo; a child; the road.

places.name: The Bound Urns
sources: uesp:Lore:Argonian (blasphemers bound to an urn and denied return)

why.founding: The dead who are denied return to the Hist are bound into urns, and the urns have to be kept somewhere nobody will break them by accident.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry rock shelter on the rim above the swamp — dry enough to keep clay, remote enough to be forgotten deliberately.
why.occupantsMotive: An officeholder from Greylight visits twice a year to check the seals and says nothing about it afterwards.
why.pressures: There are urns here from the last decade, which means the punishment is still being handed down.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be emptied by anyone who decided the sentences had run long enough — which is not a decision anyone has the standing to make.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: deliberately outside a village's normal ground

vibe.silhouette: A dry overhang with two hundred sealed clay urns in rows on ledges, oldest at the back, newest at the front.
vibe.palette: Clay red-brown, rock grey, and the black wax of the seals.
vibe.materials: Fired clay and wax; the ledges are cut, minimally, into the rock.
vibe.signatureFeature: The dates: the front row is recent, which is the detail that changes what the place is.
vibe.condition: Dry, ordered, inspected.
vibe.approach: The overhang is invisible from below; you climb to it, and then the rows go back into the dark.
vibe.senses: Very dry air; your own voice deadened; a faint sound from the front row that you will decide was wind.

why.founding: A kilometre of open stone causeway in a province of storms needs one place to stop, and the obligation supplies it.
why.siteAdvantages: At the causeway's mid-point, built out sideways on its own small platform.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by rota from Stormhold's south quarter, which regards the duty as an honour and competes for it.
why.pressures: Pilgrim numbers have risen and the rota families are quietly out of pocket.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be an embarrassment to the whole city if it were ever found cold.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a route, with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities
preferences: a fuel store larger than the room
a lamp on the causeway side

vibe.silhouette: A single small room built out from the side of a stone causeway, with a lamp bracket and no door.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, lamp yellow, and open bog in every direction.
vibe.materials: Stone below to the causeway's own construction, reed and mud above — the only such hybrid in the north.
vibe.signatureFeature: The fuel store, which is bigger than the room, because on this causeway fuel is the whole point.
vibe.condition: Immaculate; the rota families compete on the quality of the fuel.
vibe.approach: It is the only thing standing on a kilometre of straight stone, visible from both ends.
vibe.senses: Wind that stops the moment you step inside; fire; the causeway ringing under passing feet.

places.name: The Charge Pond
sources: docs/quests/20-world-provisions.md §12b (wamasu electrify the water around them)

why.founding: A wamasu holds a deep pond and curses all the water around it to deadly convulsions, which is canon and is also a swimming rule.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep still water fed from below, with no outflow strong enough to move anything out of it.
why.occupantsMotive: The creature is here because the pond is deep and quiet; everything else is here by accident and briefly.
why.pressures: The villages' offerings have made the pond a place people approach on purpose, which is new and unwise.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not change. Fixed danger means the pond stays lethal whatever the player is.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: a held pond, still and avoided
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: a district hazard; villages route around it

vibe.silhouette: A perfectly still black pond ringed by dead standing trees, with nothing floating on it and nothing on the surface at all.
vibe.palette: Black water, bleached dead timber, and an occasional blue-white flash under the surface.
vibe.materials: Nothing built. The dead trees are the architecture.
vibe.signatureFeature: The dead ring: every tree within ten metres of the water is dead standing, and beyond that they are alive.
vibe.condition: Unchanging.
vibe.approach: The dead ring of trees is visible for two hundred metres and is the only warning in the province that reads as a shape.
vibe.senses: Absolute silence, then a crack; the smell of a storm on a clear day.

places.name: The Charge Works
sources: uesp:Lore:Wamasu (hide, luminescent organs, charge-holding bones, Hist-sap insulated prods)

why.founding: A wamasu is worth more dead than any three other animals in the province, and someone has to process one when it is taken.
why.siteAdvantages: Downwind and downstream of the village, on a spit where the water can carry the waste away.
why.occupantsMotive: The works family holds the sap-insulation technique and will not teach it, which is why the works is a family and not a trade.
why.pressures: Charge-holding bone is the north's most valuable export after crystal, and Stormhold's enchanters want the supply tied up.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end with the family, and the technique with it, unless the daughter changes her mind.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: near but not on a wamasu pond
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the only reason to live this close to that water
preferences: a bone store on sap-insulated posts

occupants: one D3 taker who goes to the ponds
notableNpcSlots: the works-mother
the daughter who will not learn

vibe.silhouette: Racks of translucent hide drying in rows, and a bone store raised on posts wrapped in amber sap.
vibe.palette: Hide translucent grey-blue, amber post wraps, and a faint constant glow from the organ jars.
vibe.materials: Timber and reed on insulated footings; the sap wrapping is the only distinctive material.
vibe.signatureFeature: The organ jars, which are the works' only light source and glow without fire.
vibe.condition: Clean, careful, exact — a workshop where a mistake is fatal.
vibe.approach: The glow from the jars shows through the reed walls at night at a distance of two hundred metres.
vibe.senses: A faint crackle from the bone store; scraping; no open flames anywhere.

why.founding: The second Dres holding, abandoned when the family failed and the survivors went into Thorn's trade quarter.
why.siteAdvantages: Higher and colder than the first, on ground that turned out not to carry enough grazing.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; the tomb is still sealed and the Argonian neighbours will not touch a sealed tomb of any people.
why.pressures: The compound is being taken apart for timber by everyone except its rightful heirs.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be reclaimed instantly if a Dres heir arrived — and one exists, in Thorn.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the Tear road and the Morrowind frontier
hardConstraints: a failed upland holding with a sealed tomb

vibe.silhouette: A roofless walled square with a sealed black door at one end and the roof timbers visibly missing.
vibe.palette: Grey render cracking, black door, nettle green inside the walls.
vibe.materials: Velothi stonework being quietly dismantled; the tomb door untouched and clean.
vibe.signatureFeature: The contrast: the compound stripped to the walls and the tomb door not even dusty.
vibe.condition: Ruined above ground, intact below.
vibe.approach: The square walls show on the ridge from a long way, and the door does not show at all until you are inside.
vibe.senses: Wind through a roofless square; nettles; a very solid silence at the door.

places.name: The Prospectors' Camp

why.founding: The Silyanorn seams will not last, and everyone in the north knows it, so people are out looking for the next one.
why.siteAdvantages: On the rim scree above the root gallery, where the rock is exposed and the seams would show if they were there.
why.occupantsMotive: The prospectors are speculators on their own account, sinking their own money, and half of them are cutters from Crystalgate.
why.pressures: They have found nothing in four seasons, and two have started mapping the root gallery instead.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty overnight if a seam were struck, and Crystalgate would move to it.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near a known extraction district

notableNpcSlots: the cutter who staked everything
the one mapping the gallery instead

vibe.silhouette: A scatter of test pits across a scree slope, each with a stake in it, and one cook shelter shared by people who are competitors.
vibe.palette: Scree grey, stake wood pale, one canvas awning.
vibe.materials: Canvas, stakes and stacked stone wind-breaks; nothing anyone intends to keep.
vibe.signatureFeature: The claim stakes: forty of them across the slope, each with a name and a date, most of the dates old.
vibe.condition: Provisional, four seasons deep, quietly failing.
vibe.approach: The white stakes on grey scree read from the valley track at a kilometre.
vibe.senses: Hammering on rock at intervals; wind; a shared kettle.

places.name: The Delta Byre

why.founding: The Tear road runs on guar and the delta breeds the one strain that will work wet ground without foundering.
why.siteAdvantages: Brackish delta grazing on firm islands — poor for crops, ideal for a Glowgill herd.
why.occupantsMotive: The byre breeds and sells to both provinces' caravans, which makes it the least political business in the north.
why.pressures: The strain is theirs and unpatented; a Dres factor has twice tried to buy the breeding stock outright.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be bought out within a decade unless the family keeps refusing, which the daughter may not.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: serves a coastal settlement's transport
hardConstraints: brackish delta grazing on firm islands

occupants: a herd that swims between islands
notableNpcSlots: the breeder
the Dres factor who keeps returning

vibe.silhouette: Rail pens on three low islands with guar swimming between them, and a byre built out over the water on piles.
vibe.palette: Guar hide green-grey, water silver, rail timber black with salt.
vibe.materials: Split rail and piled timber; the pens are half in the water, which no other byre in Tamriel is.
vibe.signatureFeature: The swimming crossings: the herd is driven from island to island through the channel, twice a day.
vibe.condition: Salt-eaten and constantly replaced; nothing here lasts five years.
vibe.approach: You see guar swimming before you see any structure — the cue is the animals, not the buildings.
vibe.senses: Guar calling across water; splashing; salt and dung.

places.name: The Divers' Landing
sources: docs/world/00-core.md (Argonian physiology materially changes underwater play)

why.founding: A lake with a drowned xanmeer in it produces divers, and divers produce a landing where what they raise is sorted and sold.
why.siteAdvantages: The nearest firm bank to the drowned terrace, with deep water two boat-lengths out.
why.occupantsMotive: The divers work the terrace and argue about which chambers are permissible, in public, constantly.
why.pressures: Greylight's minders have declared parts of it off limits, and the landing has no way to enforce or ignore that cleanly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be shut by the villages together if a Hist chamber were ever stripped.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: always paired with drowned ground it works

notableNpcSlots: the sorting elder who rules on each piece

vibe.silhouette: Two shelves under a reed roof — one long and full, one short and almost empty — and a lake going dark green ten metres out.
vibe.palette: Wet stone grey, weed green, reed roof, and lake water on everything.
vibe.materials: Timber racks and a reed shelter; every object under it came up from below.
vibe.signatureFeature: The two shelves: what may be sold, and what must go back. The short shelf is the interesting one.
vibe.condition: Working and permanently wet.
vibe.mood: Argumentative, amphibious, scrupulous in a way that is being tested.
vibe.approach: The landing is the only break in a reed shore for a kilometre and is visible from the water.
vibe.senses: Dripping; a diver surfacing; an argument about a fitting.

why.founding: The northern lake drops three metres in the dry season and exposes ground that spends most of the year underwater.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow shelf on the lake's north side, the largest area exposed by the annual drawdown.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives on it, by definition; everybody uses it for the eight weeks it exists.
why.pressures: What the water uncovers changes each year, and includes things people would rather stayed covered.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be permanent ground if the lake ever fell for good, and the villages consider that a nightmare, not a windfall.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the lake region's signature seasonal event
hardConstraints: a shelf exposed by annual drawdown

vibe.silhouette: A wide plain of cracked grey mud with the lake a long way out, and things standing up out of it that are not rocks.
vibe.palette: Crack-pattern grey, weed black drying to brown, distant water.
vibe.materials: Nothing built. Whatever the lake gives back is the content, and it is different every year.
vibe.signatureFeature: The strandline: a curve of debris marking where the water stopped this year, and last year's above it.
vibe.condition: Reset annually.
vibe.mood: Bleak, revelatory, faintly indecent — the lake with its clothes off.
vibe.approach: From the shore the water is simply somewhere else, which is the whole reveal.
vibe.senses: Mud cracking underfoot; gulls a long way off; wind with nothing to cross.

why.founding: Naga range further north in the wet season than anyone admits, and a caravan road through wet ground is a hunting lane.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the Tear road's delta section runs between two channels — a place a road cannot leave.
why.occupantsMotive: They camp for the season and take what passes; this is not banditry as the road understands it.
why.pressures: Thorn's levy sweeps the section twice a year and finds an empty camp both times.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not be here at all in a dry year, and the road forgets between them.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: commands traffic and offers an escape
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on a route with traffic worth robbing

vibe.silhouette: Nothing on the road; in the reeds beside it, trampled beds and drying racks, and a great deal of bone.
vibe.palette: Reed gold, bone white, water black.
vibe.materials: No structure at all — beds pressed in the reeds and racks of lashed cane.
vibe.signatureFeature: The racks: what has been taken off the road, drying in plain sight thirty metres from it.
vibe.condition: Seasonal; the camp is remade each wet season in a slightly different reed bed.
vibe.approach: From the road, nothing. The cue is the smell of drying meat and it arrives from the wrong side.
vibe.senses: Reeds moving against the wind; nothing spoken; water.

why.founding: A xanmeer whose ground subsided into the lake, taking a complete Merethic building down with it intact.
why.siteAdvantages: A lake basin over soft ground — the province's hydrology drowns what it does not flood.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing lives in it. The nearest village dives it for stone fittings and considers this different from looting a standing xanmeer.
why.pressures: The distinction is not universally accepted, and Greylight has said so.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a serious quarrel the day someone brought up something that was clearly a Hist chamber's fitting.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in drowned country; often near a drowned village
preferences: an intact interior with air pockets

vibe.silhouette: One corner of a terrace breaking the lake surface like a step, and beneath it a whole building in green light.
vibe.palette: Surface silver, green underwater light, pale stone going blue with depth.
vibe.materials: Xanmeer ashlar, entirely intact, with lake weed picking out every carved line.
vibe.signatureFeature: The building is complete: you swim its stairs and doorways as they were built, which nothing on land here offers.
vibe.condition: Perfectly preserved by the water that ruined it.
vibe.approach: From the surface it is one stone step in open water; the reveal is entirely on the dive.
vibe.senses: Underwater silence; your own breath held; stone under your hands.

why.founding: The obligation applies in field country too, and in field country the comers are mostly people who have just lost an Owing case.
why.siteAdvantages: At the edge of the terraces where the road from Thorn's court comes out into the fields.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by Saltmarch's rota; the Dunmer households take their turn, which took a generation to arrange.
why.pressures: The field-owners regard it as a shelter for runaways and have said so; the villages have declined to discuss it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a flashpoint the first time an overseer took someone out of it.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a route, with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities
hardConstraints: at the field country's edge on the court road

vibe.silhouette: A round house at a field corner with the door facing the court road and a fire always laid.
vibe.palette: Thatch, saltrice silver on three sides, road dust on the fourth.
vibe.materials: Mud, wattle and reed, with the Dunmer rota's contribution visible as a lacquered lintel nobody comments on.
vibe.signatureFeature: The lacquered lintel — a foreign household's mark on a house that belongs to nobody.
vibe.condition: Kept up by eight households in turn, so the repairs are in eight hands.
vibe.approach: It sits at a field corner in the open with the door towards the road, which is a statement.
vibe.senses: Wind through saltrice; a fire; someone not explaining why they are here.

places.name: Field Gate

why.founding: Thorn's field-owners keep a levy, and a levy has to be quartered where the fields end and the road to Morrowind begins.
why.siteAdvantages: The gap between the terrace country and the pass road — the only line an approach from the north must cross.
why.occupantsMotive: The levy exists to protect titles, not people, and its officers are the field-owners' sons.
why.pressures: Half the levy are Dunmer, which is either sensible recruiting or a serious mistake depending on who is asked.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be disbanded within a year if Thorn's title disputes were ever settled, and nobody expects that.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: at a crossing or a road
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: always paired with a fort, occupied or not
hardConstraints: the gap between the fields and the pass road

notableNpcSlots: the captain who is a field-owner's second son
the Dunmer serjeant everybody actually obeys

vibe.silhouette: A drill ground with a town on three sides of it and open fields on the fourth, and shellback armour drying on every rail.
vibe.palette: Shell-plate grey-brown, saltrice silver beyond, dust.
vibe.materials: Mud-brick billets around a beaten drill square; the only fortification is a fence.
vibe.signatureFeature: The shell racks: the levy's armour is grown, not forged, and it is racked outside to cure in the sun.
vibe.condition: Serviceable, crowded, unfortified because it is a levy and not a garrison.
vibe.approach: The drill counting carries across the open fields for a kilometre before anything is visible.
vibe.senses: Drill; shell plates knocking; two languages of complaint.

why.founding: The first ground the Flu filled, in the first season, before anyone understood what was happening.
why.siteAdvantages: On the terrace below Stormhold's south gate, because at the time nobody could carry the dead further.
why.occupantsMotive: The city maintains it because it cannot not; the maintenance is done at night and nobody says why.
why.pressures: Kothringi dead are buried here alongside Argonian dead — a mixing that neither people's rite permits and both accepted.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the north's central memorial if the city could bear to make it one.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village
hardConstraints: within sight of the city gate

vibe.silhouette: A wide flat terrace of grass with grave-stakes at one end and Kothringi cairns at the other, and nothing between them.
vibe.palette: Stake grey, cairn grey, grass, and the city's terraces looming above.
vibe.materials: Grave-stakes and cairns in the same ground, neither adapted to the other.
vibe.signatureFeature: The empty middle: a strip of unmarked grass between two traditions that were buried side by side.
vibe.condition: Mown, edged, and never spoken about.
vibe.approach: It is the first thing you pass leaving the south gate and the last thing anyone will discuss.
vibe.senses: The city above; stakes knocking; nothing else.

why.founding: The Flu began at Stormhold, and the north cordoned itself against its own city — the only such line drawn from the inside out.
why.siteAdvantages: A ring of markers at a day's walk from the city, following the ground where the channels make a natural boundary.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody keeps it. Nobody has crossed a marker on foot in three hundred years without noticing they did it.
why.pressures: Stormhold has never formally acknowledged that the line was drawn against Stormhold.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a diplomatic incident if anyone re-marked it, which is why nobody has.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: uses water as part of the line where it can
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: encircles a plague-abandoned village or a cairn field
hardConstraints: a ring at a day's walk from the city

vibe.silhouette: Marker stones set at intervals with their carved faces turned away from the city, not towards it.
vibe.palette: Lichen grey, marsh green, nothing else.
vibe.materials: Undressed set stone — the same grammar as every cordon in the province, and the only one pointing inward.
vibe.signatureFeature: The orientation: every marker faces out from Stormhold, which tells you who was being kept in.
vibe.condition: Fallen in places, never re-set, never removed.
vibe.mood: Accusatory, patient, entirely silent about it.
vibe.approach: You cross it on the Tear road without noticing and then see the next stone.
vibe.senses: Wind; the road; a long absence of anything else.

places.name: The Freed Rows

why.founding: When the pens emptied, the people in them had nowhere to be; a shelter grew where they stopped walking.
why.siteAdvantages: A day south of the pen yard — precisely as far as a column of exhausted people got on the first day.
why.occupantsMotive: It persists because people still arrive: Owing runaways now, rather than freed slaves, and the distinction is thinner every year.
why.pressures: The Owing brokers regard it as a receiving house for stolen labour and say so in Thorn's court.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be closed by a court order the day the Owing were ruled property — which is exactly the case being argued.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: within a day of a hard owing district, out of its sight
hardConstraints: one day's walk from the pen yard

occupants: one strong D3 who watches the road
notableNpcSlots: the shelter-holder
the runaway whose Owing is being litigated

vibe.silhouette: Three long open-sided shelters and a board at the road end with names painted on it, hundreds of them.
vibe.palette: Thatch, whitewash on the board, and the paint of a hundred different hands.
vibe.materials: Mud, reed and open frames — nothing here has a door, deliberately.
vibe.signatureFeature: The name board: everyone who has passed through, written by themselves if they can write and by someone else if not.
vibe.condition: Well kept, permanently under-provisioned, constantly extended.
vibe.approach: The board is at the road edge and is the first thing you read, before you see the shelters.
vibe.senses: A lot of people sleeping; a cooking fire that never goes out; someone reading names aloud.

places.name: The Last Landing

why.founding: The north-eastern river is navigable to exactly one point, and everything that goes further inland is carried.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock sill across the channel: deep water below it, boulders above, and a bank on both sides.
why.occupantsMotive: The landing exists to change cargo from hull to back, and every trade here is a version of that.
why.pressures: The porters and the boat crews price against each other twice a day, in public, loudly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move upstream permanently the year anyone blasted the sill, which two generations have proposed.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the hinge between a boat lane and a land route; a mandatory node

notableNpcSlots: the landing-holder who sets the carry rate

vibe.silhouette: A quay with masts at it, a rock sill in white water just upstream, and a porter yard above the sill with no boats at all.
vibe.palette: River green below the sill, white over it, and the two halves of the settlement quite different colours.
vibe.materials: Stone quay below, timber and reed yard above — the settlement changes material at the sill.
vibe.signatureFeature: The sill itself: you can stand on it and touch a laden boat on one side and a laden porter on the other.
vibe.condition: Busy, worn, structurally split in two.
vibe.approach: The white water is audible from a long way and the masts appear below it.
vibe.senses: Water over rock; ropes; two crews shouting rates at each other.

why.founding: A xanmeer whose building stopped mid-course when the Duskfall came, and which the province has kept unfinished on purpose ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: A rise on the northern edge of the swamp, chosen when the builders still thought there would be time.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. Nearby villages bring their young here to be told why nobody builds in stone any more.
why.pressures: Mazzatun is four days east and building in stone right now, which makes this site's lesson urgent again.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be completed by the Xit-Xaht in a heartbeat if they were ever offered it.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in xanmeer country; contrasts directly with the tended and sealed ones
preferences: dressed blocks lying where they were left
a teaching place at the base

vibe.silhouette: Three complete terraces and a fourth with its top course half laid, blocks still on the ramp behind it.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, green ramp, and a sharp horizontal line where the building stops.
vibe.materials: Xanmeer ashlar, with the construction ramp — earth and timber — still in place after four thousand years because nobody would remove it.
vibe.signatureFeature: The half-laid course: five blocks set, one lifted and not placed, lying where it was dropped.
vibe.condition: Preserved exactly as abandoned, deliberately.
vibe.mood: Instructive, sombre, unfinished in a way that is the point.
vibe.approach: The flat top and the ramp read against the sky from the channels — a xanmeer silhouette that is subtly wrong.
vibe.senses: Wind over an open terrace; a teacher's voice; children being quiet.

places.name: The Monsoon Boom
sources: uesp:Lore:Black Marsh (roads close in the monsoon)

why.founding: The Tear road's delta section goes under in the monsoon and Thorn closes it, because the alternative is losing caravans.
why.siteAdvantages: The lowest crossing of the terrace country, where the delta backs up first.
why.occupantsMotive: The barrier is worked by the paddy gate-holders, who are already there for the gates.
why.pressures: Dunmer caravans have twice ignored it and once been right, which is the whole problem.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be unnecessary if the road were embanked, and Thorn's owners will not pay for a road they do not own.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on a road that has a wet-season alternative

vibe.silhouette: A floating timber boom across a road, chained at both ends, with a depth gauge beside it painted in bands.
vibe.palette: Warning bands in white and black, brown floodwater, grey sky.
vibe.materials: A chained boom and one painted gauge post; nothing else is built.
vibe.signatureFeature: The gauge's top band, painted in a different, older paint than the rest — a level reached once.
vibe.condition: Crude and functional.
vibe.approach: In the dry it is a chain lying in the dust; in the wet it is a boom on water with no road visible.
vibe.senses: Rain; the chain; water moving over a road surface.

places.name: The North Post

why.founding: Argonia checks what comes down the Tear road, and what it is checking for is people being taken north.
why.siteAdvantages: Below the pass on the Argonian side, at the first point where a caravan can be stopped without being on a slope.
why.occupantsMotive: The keepers count heads out and heads back, a practice begun after the invasion and never repealed.
why.pressures: House Dres's successors find the count insulting; the keepers find that satisfying.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned if the Owing were ever abolished, because the Owing is what the count is really about.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: spaced along the border; gaps are the point

notableNpcSlots: the head-counter

vibe.silhouette: A gate of two posts and a rope, a tally house, and a stone with notches on it beside the road.
vibe.palette: Rope, unpainted timber, and one very old notched stone.
vibe.materials: Timber and reed; the notched stone is the only permanent object and it is not a building.
vibe.signatureFeature: The head-count stone: notches for people going north, and a shorter column for people coming back.
vibe.condition: Simple, kept, undramatic.
vibe.approach: The rope across the road is visible at fifty metres and the stone is at knee height beside it.
vibe.senses: A tally called aloud; caravan noise; the rope being lowered.

why.founding: Thorn's field-owners need somewhere to put a debtor between the field and the court, and will not build a gaol because Argonians do not.
why.siteAdvantages: In a field-owner's stock yard on the Thorn road, roofed and out of the weather, which they mention.
why.occupantsMotive: The overseers use it for a night at a time, which is legal, and sometimes for longer, which is not tested.
why.pressures: The Freed Rows keep a tally of who goes in and who comes out, and the counts do not always match.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be filled in the day Thorn's court defined waiting — a case the Chainbreakers are building.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: attached to a hard-owing estate or crossing
hardConstraints: a roofed pit inside a private yard

vibe.silhouette: A roofed pit in the corner of a working stock yard, with a plank floor over it and a gap for air.
vibe.palette: Straw, dung, timber, and one dark gap.
vibe.materials: Timber and mud; the pit is older than the yard around it and nobody knows who dug it.
vibe.signatureFeature: The air gap, deliberately at boot height, so anyone in the yard can be spoken to and not seen.
vibe.condition: In constant light use.
vibe.approach: You would take it for a root store, which is what the overseers call it.
vibe.senses: Yard work above; a voice at boot height.

places.name: The North Relay

why.founding: The two northern cities do not trust each other's messengers, so a neutral relay stands between them and both pay it.
why.siteAdvantages: Exactly midway on the northern road, on ground belonging to neither city's hinterland.
why.occupantsMotive: The relay families keep neutrality as an inheritance and refuse to read, carry sealed writs unopened, and are paid twice.
why.pressures: Both cities have tried to buy an exception; the refusals are part of the family's standing.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse the moment one refusal was proven to have been sold.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay
preferences: two letter boxes, one per city

notableNpcSlots: the relay elder

vibe.silhouette: Two identical letter boxes on two posts, a hammock frame between them, and nothing else for a kilometre.
vibe.palette: Weathered post grey, two different city seals, marsh green.
vibe.materials: Two waxed boxes and a reed shelter; deliberately nothing lockable and nothing city-built.
vibe.signatureFeature: The symmetry: the two boxes are identical and exactly the same distance from the shelter, and that is a policy.
vibe.condition: Maintained daily; the boxes are replaced together or not at all.
vibe.approach: Two posts on an empty road — you would take it for a boundary marker.
vibe.senses: Somebody leaving at a run; wind; a box lid.

why.founding: The root layer reaches its northern limit here, and where it thins over cold rim ground it leaves galleries that are colder and drier than any in the south.
why.siteAdvantages: Between the swamp's edge and the rim's stone, where roots run over rock instead of mud.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing keeps it; the prospectors' camp above uses the first chamber as a store.
why.pressures: It is the only root gallery in the province with a stone floor, which makes it navigable and makes it dangerous differently.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the north's cave system if anyone mapped it, and the prospectors have started to.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect, and that connection is the map
hardConstraints: roots over rock rather than mud

vibe.silhouette: A gallery with a living root ceiling and a bare rock floor, which is a combination that exists nowhere else.
vibe.palette: Root brown above, grey stone below, and a cold blue light at two collapses.
vibe.materials: No construction; the prospectors' store boxes are the only made objects.
vibe.signatureFeature: The floor: dry stone under a wet ceiling, so it drips continuously onto rock and the sound never stops.
vibe.condition: The upper chambers stable; the lower ones changing as roots shift.
vibe.mood: Cold, echoing, unlike the rest of the province underground.
vibe.approach: The mouth is behind the prospectors' camp and looks like a store, which it partly is.
vibe.senses: Dripping onto stone with a hard echo; roots creaking; a draught from deeper in.
