places.name: The North Vista
sources: world/sources/sites/candidate-sites.md (a quarter of the interesting ground is on the rim)
docs/world/00-core.md (large logical surfaces climbable by default)

why.founding: The rim is the only place in Argonia with a long view, and one ledge above the pass looks back over the whole northern marsh.
why.siteAdvantages: A ridge nose above the Tear road, high enough to clear the haze on a cold morning.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody keeps it; couriers use it to check the weather and travellers climb it for the reason anyone climbs anything.
why.pressures: It is the one place from which the province's scale is legible, and almost nobody in the province has been there.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not change, and does not need to.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: placed where the visibility raster shows a dead zone
hardConstraints: a ledge above the haze line

vibe.silhouette: A flat ledge the size of a room, a cairn on it, and the entire northern marsh laid out below in bands of haze.
vibe.palette: Rock grey underfoot, and below, every green the province has, fading blue to the horizon.
vibe.materials: One cairn. Nothing else, and nothing else is wanted.
vibe.signatureFeature: The cairn's contents: travellers leave one small thing each, and nobody takes anything.
vibe.condition: Unchanged except by the cairn growing.
vibe.approach: Two hours of climbing with no view at all, and then the ledge and everything at once.
vibe.senses: Wind; nothing else; the marsh is too far away to be heard, which is itself extraordinary.

why.founding: The Nisswo walk the north too, though less often, and the villages keep a house ready for a preacher who may not come this year.
why.siteAdvantages: On the Bogmother causeway road, where the pilgrim traffic already passes.
why.occupantsMotive: It is maintained by villages who would not describe themselves as devout and would be offended to be called otherwise.
why.pressures: No Nisswo has come for three years, and the house is still swept weekly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be maintained anyway. That is the whole point of the institution.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: between villages on a preaching circuit

vibe.silhouette: A small house with a black door, standing open, with a bed made and a fire laid and nobody in it.
vibe.palette: Black door, ochre wall, and the pale of clean bedding.
vibe.materials: Mud and reed, plain, and swept to a standard the villages' own houses do not meet.
vibe.signatureFeature: The made bed: turned down, three years running, by people taking turns.
vibe.condition: Immaculate and unused.
vibe.approach: The black door on an empty road, standing open, is the cue and it is enough.
vibe.senses: Wind through an open door; absolutely nothing else.

why.founding: A xanmeer that was opened, looted and left, and has since been occupied by people with no claim to it at all.
why.siteAdvantages: On the channel network within a day of the trunk route — accessible, which is exactly why it was broken.
why.occupantsMotive: The current occupants are river thieves who like stone walls and do not care whose they are.
why.pressures: Greylight has asked twice for it to be cleared and Stormhold has not answered.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be re-tended within a season if a tribe with a claim took it back, which is a live quest.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in a district with other xanmeer, showing the range of states

vibe.silhouette: A stepped terrace with a hole knocked in one face and cook-smoke coming out of the top of it.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, black smoke, and washing strung between two terraces.
vibe.materials: Xanmeer ashlar with hide, rope and stolen canvas rigged across it.
vibe.signatureFeature: The washing line: domestic laundry strung across a sacred terrace, which is the whole offence in one image.
vibe.condition: Structurally fine, ritually destroyed, casually inhabited.
vibe.approach: Smoke from a xanmeer terrace reads for a kilometre and means exactly one thing to anyone local.
vibe.senses: Voices echoing in stone; a dog; someone cooking where nobody should.

why.founding: The Barsaebic Ayleid settlement that Stormhold was built on top of, whose outer compound lies beyond the city's ravines.
why.siteAdvantages: The same dry shelf the city occupies, continuing north where the city stopped building.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies it. The city quarries the undercity and ignores the surface work entirely, which suits the surviving structures.
why.pressures: It is the only part of Silyanorn nobody is licensed to dig, purely because nobody has thought to ask.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be quarried within a year of anyone realising the licence covers only the galleries.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in the north and west, where the Barsaebic Ayleids went
preferences: a clear line to the city

vibe.silhouette: A white arcade standing in scrub within sight of the city, untouched while the ground beneath the city is being emptied.
vibe.palette: Bone white, scrub green, and Stormhold's terraces grey in the distance.
vibe.materials: Barsaebic Ayleid surface masonry — the same hand as the galleries below the city, in daylight.
vibe.signatureFeature: The intactness: the only unquarried Silyanorn stone, and it is the piece everyone can see.
vibe.condition: Weathered but unrobbed.
vibe.approach: It is plainly visible from Stormhold's north terrace, which is why nobody has ever gone to look.
vibe.senses: Wind through an arcade; the city faintly; nothing else.

places.name: The Pass Station

why.founding: The Tear road crosses the rim at one saddle, and the saddle kills people in winter, so both provinces have paid for a station on it.
why.siteAdvantages: The saddle's crown, where the road is at its highest and there is no lee at all.
why.occupantsMotive: Two keepers hold it under an arrangement between Thorn's field-owners and a Dres factor, which is the only functioning cross-border institution in the north.
why.pressures: Neither side will pay for the roof, so the roof is the worst part of the building.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse as an institution if either province stopped paying — and the keepers have a bad feeling.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the only crossings of the rim; each one is strategically singular

occupants: D3 on the road above the station in weather
notableNpcSlots: the two keepers, who are paid by different provinces and share a bed

vibe.silhouette: A stone hut on a bare saddle with a line of tall poles running away into the cloud on both sides.
vibe.palette: Stone grey, cloud white, and the poles painted alternately in two provinces' colours.
vibe.materials: Dry stone with a bad turf roof; the poles are the only maintained thing.
vibe.signatureFeature: The pole line: painted in Thorn's colours on one half and Tear's on the other, meeting at the hut.
vibe.condition: Walls excellent, roof appalling, a metaphor everyone here has already made.
vibe.approach: The poles are the cue and they are the only wayfinding on the pass in weather.
vibe.senses: Wind that does not stop; a bell rung on the hour in fog; two accents.

why.founding: Slavery ended; the buildings did not. This is where the Dres assembled and shipped people north for four centuries.
why.siteAdvantages: On the road below the pass, at the last point where a column could be held overnight.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. It is used as a cattle pen by a neighbouring holding, which is either healing or obscene depending who you ask.
why.pressures: It is structurally excellent and there is a live argument about pulling it down.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be demolished tomorrow if the district could agree, and the district cannot.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the old Morrowind-border trade line
preferences: ring bolts still in the walls

vibe.silhouette: A stone-walled yard with a loading ramp at one end and iron ring bolts in the walls at two heights.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, rust stains under every bolt, and green fodder trodden into the floor.
vibe.materials: Velothi stonework, built to last, and used now for animals.
vibe.signatureFeature: The two heights of ring bolt: adult and child. Nobody who has seen it needs it explained.
vibe.condition: In excellent repair, because it is in use.
vibe.approach: It looks exactly like a stock yard from the road, which is the point at which you understand it.
vibe.senses: Cattle; wind in a walled yard; iron rings knocking stone.

places.name: The Permit Dig

why.founding: Cyrodilic Collections keeps an alcove at Stormhold, and an alcove implies a dig somewhere it can defend as lawful.
why.siteAdvantages: On Outer Silyanorn's edge, on the one parcel the city was willing to licence.
why.occupantsMotive: The Collections dig to return; the vicecanons licence it to keep an eye on it; the diggers dig for wages.
why.pressures: The parcel they were given is deliberately the least interesting ground on the site, and both parties know it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move onto the arcade the moment the licence was widened, which the city will not do.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: always beside a ruin
hardConstraints: a licensed parcel beside a ruin
preferences: a permit posted at the gate

notableNpcSlots: the alcove-keeper
the city's observer who writes everything down

vibe.silhouette: A fenced parcel of trenches with a permit board at the gate, and the far more interesting ruin plainly visible beyond the fence.
vibe.palette: Canvas white, spoil brown, and white Ayleid stone just out of reach.
vibe.materials: Canvas and rope inside a woven fence; the fence is the point of the place.
vibe.signatureFeature: The permit board, with the licensed boundary drawn on it, and everyone standing at the fence looking over.
vibe.condition: Neat, orderly, frustrated.
vibe.mood: Diligent, hemmed in, wryly funny about it.
vibe.approach: The tent and the fence read from the city road; the fence line is the thing you notice.
vibe.senses: Trowels; a city clerk's pen; conversation about the fence.

provisions: a licensed dig with a hard boundary

places.name: The Pilots' Rest

why.founding: Boat crews on the trunk route need a bed that is not their own hull, and the channel villages will not take strangers overnight.
why.siteAdvantages: Built out over the water at a wide bend where six boats can lie alongside at once.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper was a pilot, retired from it, and sells the knowledge she no longer sells the labour for.
why.pressures: The channel pilots at Channel Cross regard her as competition and her rates as a betrayal.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be bought out by the pilots' families if she ever agreed to sell, and she will not.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a route, with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement
hardConstraints: a wide bend with alongside mooring

occupants: D2 who came upriver for a reason
notableNpcSlots: the retired pilot

vibe.silhouette: A long veranda on piles over a bend, with six mooring rings and lamps at each of them.
vibe.palette: Lamp yellow on black water, reed roof, and a lot of hulls at night.
vibe.materials: Stilt construction with an unusually long unbroken veranda — a shape driven entirely by mooring length.
vibe.signatureFeature: The six lamps, lit in order as boats arrive, so from upstream you can count who is already in.
vibe.condition: Well built, wet, constantly re-decked at the mooring edge.
vibe.approach: The lamp count is readable from six hundred metres upstream — information, not just a cue.
vibe.senses: Hulls knocking; a hammock creaking; talk about water levels.

places.name: The Salt and Shell

why.founding: A caravan house at the field-country crossroads, where a Dunmer trader and an Argonian porter will both find something they can eat.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the Tear road meets the terrace lanes, with room for beasts.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper cooks two cuisines badly and is loved for the attempt.
why.pressures: The levy drinks here and the smugglers drink here and the keeper seats them by shift.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close if the Tear road ever went quiet, and the district would mourn.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a route, with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement
hardConstraints: at a road junction in the field country

notableNpcSlots: the keeper who cooks both badly

vibe.silhouette: A long house with two chimneys, two doors and beast lines down both sides of the yard.
vibe.palette: Smoke-brown, two different door paints, saltrice silver beyond the yard.
vibe.materials: Argonian frame with a Dunmer-style second hearth added at the far end, badly.
vibe.signatureFeature: Two hearths in one room, each with its own cook pot and its own regulars.
vibe.condition: Extended twice, sagging in the middle, warm.
vibe.approach: Two chimneys smoking at once is the cue and it is visible across the flat fields.
vibe.senses: Two languages, one argument; beasts in the yard; a great deal of cooking.

places.name: The Salt Ledge

why.founding: The head-count at the border post is exactly why an uncounted route over the rim exists.
why.siteAdvantages: A ledge line running parallel to the pass a kilometre east, wide enough for a person and not for a beast.
why.occupantsMotive: The carriers move salt north and, when the price is right, people — which is what the count was meant to stop.
why.pressures: Both provinces know it is there; neither wants the diplomatic cost of closing it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close in a week if the head-count were dropped, which is the argument the smugglers make.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: none; this is the dry route
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: beside a pass, out of sight of its post
hardConstraints: a ledge parallel to the legal pass
preferences: a lookout with a line to the pass

notableNpcSlots: the carrier who will name a price for anything

vibe.silhouette: A ledge a pace wide running along a rock face, with salt spilled white in the cracks along its whole length.
vibe.palette: White salt in grey rock, and a drop.
vibe.materials: Nothing built but rope anchors and a hide cache under an overhang.
vibe.signatureFeature: The spilled salt: centuries of loads scraping the wall have left a white line you can follow in the dark.
vibe.condition: Unmaintained and heavily used.
vibe.approach: The white line is the path and it is invisible from anywhere except on it.
vibe.senses: Boots on grit; wind; the pass bell far below and to the west.

places.name: The Shoal Bank

why.founding: A submerged bar off the delta concentrates fish, and the north's protein comes off it.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the river's silt meets tidal water, three metres down over two hundred metres of bank.
why.occupantsMotive: Six villages fish it under a marker system that is entirely oral and entirely respected.
why.pressures: The Dunmer boats out of Thorn have started fishing it and do not know the markers.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be fished out in a decade under any system that could not exclude newcomers.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: contested between two coastal settlements
hardConstraints: a submerged bar at a silt-tide boundary

occupants: D3 in the deeper water beyond the bank

vibe.silhouette: Open water with a colour change in it, and four boats sitting in a line along an edge you cannot see.
vibe.palette: Two greens meeting in a line; boat hulls; birds working the edge.
vibe.materials: Nothing built on the water; the marks are two poles and a tree on shore, lined up.
vibe.signatureFeature: The transit: you find the bank by lining up a pole with a tree, and if you cannot, you are not local.
vibe.condition: Unchanging; the marks are maintained.
vibe.approach: The birds working the edge are visible before the boats are.
vibe.senses: Nets; gulls; a hull knocking in a swell.

places.name: The Shut Village

why.founding: A village that shut itself in during the Flu, survived, and never fully opened again — the practice outlived the reason by three centuries.
why.siteAdvantages: On an island in the channels with one causeway, which is why shutting was possible at all.
why.occupantsMotive: They keep the practice because it worked once; visitors are received at the causeway's outer end and not past it.
why.pressures: The village is inbred, dwindling and knows it; the Hatching Pools have sent word twice and been refused.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end within a generation either way — by opening, or by simply running out.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: deliberately just out of reach of its neighbours
hardConstraints: an island with a single causeway
preferences: a receiving post at the causeway's outer end

occupants: D2 villagers who do not come out
one D2 receiver at the outer post
notableNpcSlots: the receiver
the elder who refuses the Pools

vibe.silhouette: A village on an island seen only across two hundred metres of causeway, with a table set at the near end.
vibe.palette: Distance haze, reed gold, brown water, and a white cloth on the table.
vibe.materials: Ordinary mud and reed — the strangeness is entirely social, not architectural.
vibe.signatureFeature: The table: goods left, goods taken, and nobody within fifty metres of it while you are there.
vibe.condition: Well kept and visibly thinning; too many empty houses for the number of roofs maintained.
vibe.approach: You reach the table and are told, politely, that this is as far as the path goes.
vibe.senses: A voice calling across water; wind; no children's noise at all.

places.name: The Slumped Hamlet
sources: world/sources/sites/candidate-sites.md (sinkholes are genuinely rare — spend sparingly)

why.founding: A hamlet built over a limestone void near the rim, which took four generations to notice and one season to leave.
why.siteAdvantages: Good dry ground with a spring — which was the void's fault too, and nobody made the connection in time.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; the households moved two hundred metres and rebuilt, which is the province's standard answer.
why.pressures: The old and new hamlets are in sight of each other, and the old one is still slowly going down.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would take the new hamlet too if the void runs the way the rim's geology suggests.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: above workings or burning peat
hardConstraints: a rebuilt hamlet in sight of it

vibe.silhouette: Six houses leaning at the same angle into a shallow bowl, with a new hamlet's roofs visible over the rise behind them.
vibe.palette: Thatch gold at two angles, one right and one wrong; green bowl.
vibe.materials: Ordinary mud and reed; the tilt is the only thing distinguishing them from any village in the north.
vibe.signatureFeature: The uniform lean: every house tilts the same way by the same amount, which is far stranger than random collapse.
vibe.condition: Still standing, still moving, measurably lower each decade.
vibe.mood: Uncanny, gentle, slightly funny until you look at the crack.
vibe.approach: You see it from the new hamlet's path, and the two hamlets in one view is the whole story.
vibe.senses: Timber under slow strain; water running somewhere below; nothing living in them.

why.founding: Stormhold's waterfall has cut back into the rock and left a chamber behind the sheet, directly below the city.
why.siteAdvantages: The undercut is at the falls' centre, reachable along a ledge from the ravine's south side only.
why.occupantsMotive: The city knows about it. The Conclave uses it, and does not book it.
why.pressures: It is the only room within Stormhold's walls that is not in any of the city's plans.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be sealed by the vicecanons the day they worked out who was using it.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on a river with real relief — the rim and upland only
hardConstraints: an undercut behind a major fall
preferences: a view out through the water at the city

vibe.silhouette: A room behind a curtain of falling water, with the lights of a city visible through it, broken and moving.
vibe.palette: White water, black rock, and the city's lamps refracted into a moving smear of yellow.
vibe.materials: Nothing built but a stone bench and a lamp niche cut into the rock, both old.
vibe.signatureFeature: The view out: the city seen through its own waterfall, which is a thing perhaps forty people alive have seen.
vibe.condition: Dry, swept, and used more recently than it should be.
vibe.approach: The ledge is invisible from above and the chamber from everywhere; you are shown it or you are not.
vibe.senses: Water at a volume that guarantees privacy; a lamp guttering; footsteps you cannot hear.

places.name: The Stripped Village

why.founding: Umbriel passed north across the province in 4E 48 and took what it took; this village was under its shadow and is empty of bodies.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly on the recorded track, on ground that was perfectly good and is now avoided.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies it. The neighbouring villages keep a vigil rather than a taboo, which is a different thing.
why.pressures: There are no graves here because there were no bodies, which the vigil-keepers find harder than a massacre.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be resettled if the Waiting Vigil ever declared the dead accounted for, and they will not.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor, a legible line across the province

occupants: D3 at the village edge after dark

vibe.silhouette: An intact village with every roof sound, every door open, and no grave-stakes anywhere in or around it.
vibe.palette: Thatch faded to grey-gold, green pressing in, and an absence where the stake field should be.
vibe.materials: Ordinary mud and reed, untouched, decaying at the rate of a building nobody enters.
vibe.signatureFeature: The absent stake field: every Argonian village has one, and this village's ground is bare.
vibe.condition: Structurally sound after 150 years because nothing has taken anything.
vibe.approach: There is no cue and no path; the village simply resolves out of the trees, whole.
vibe.senses: Nothing. The silence in an intact village is the entire experience.

places.name: The Sump
sources: docs/research/settlement-type-recipes.md ('someone else moved in' is the province's characteristic condition)

why.founding: A Flu-emptied hamlet that outsiders — Dunmer refugees from the Red Year, four generations back — moved into because they did not know the taboo.
why.siteAdvantages: A drained sump with good soil, which is why it was worth settling twice.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay because it is theirs now by four generations of occupation and nobody has ever come to say otherwise.
why.pressures: Their neighbours have never once visited, and the children have started to notice.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be accepted into the district the day one neighbouring village ate a meal here.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in the country the Flu emptied; other villages avoid it
hardConstraints: a Flu-era footprint reoccupied by outsiders

notableNpcSlots: the eldest, who still calls the Red Year 'the year we left'

vibe.silhouette: Argonian house footings with Velothi timber and lacquer built up off them, and a shrine-niche in every gable.
vibe.palette: Dunmer red-brown lacquer over Argonian mud grey; ash-grey cloth; green sump.
vibe.materials: Two cultures stacked vertically: the footings are one, everything above waist height is the other.
vibe.signatureFeature: The gable niches — an ancestor shrine on a house whose foundation belongs to someone else's dead.
vibe.condition: Maintained continuously for four generations; the footings are the oldest thing and the best.
vibe.mood: Settled, slightly defensive, homesick for a place none of them has seen.
vibe.approach: The path in is overgrown from the neighbours' side and clear from the road side, which tells you everything.
vibe.senses: A different language; ash-cakes cooking; a bell that is not an Argonian bell.

why.founding: A Dunmer trader out of Tear misread the delta bar in a storm and is still on it, forty years later.
why.siteAdvantages: Hard aground on the outer bar, upright, where the tide covers her to the rail twice a day.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody salvages her: the cargo went in the first month and the hull is Dres property in a court nobody will convene.
why.pressures: The delta villages use her as a navigation mark and would object to her removal.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would break up in one bad storm season, and the villages would lose their best mark.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on a shipping approach or a hazard

vibe.silhouette: A Dunmer hull sitting upright on a bar with one mast still standing and the tide running through her rail.
vibe.palette: Weathered red hull paint, black weed to the waterline, one bleached mast.
vibe.materials: Velothi ship timber, foreign in every line — the only Dunmer object visible from open water in Argonia.
vibe.signatureFeature: The standing mast: kept upright by the villages, who have twice re-stayed it because it is their mark.
vibe.condition: Sound below the waterline, gone above the deck except the mast.
vibe.approach: The mast is the delta's principal seamark and reads at three kilometres in clear weather.
vibe.senses: Water through a hull; rigging that is not there any more; birds on the rail.

places.name: The Terrace Watch

why.founding: A crop worth this much needs watching, and the terraces are flat enough that one tower sees all eleven banks.
why.siteAdvantages: The single knoll in the terrace country, put there by geology and used ever since.
why.occupantsMotive: The watch is set by the villages in rotation at harvest and by the field-owners the rest of the year, and the two watches watch different things.
why.pressures: In harvest the tower watches for theft; out of harvest it watches for surveyors.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be pulled down by the villages if the field-owners ever manned it year-round.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: commands a route or a channel
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: must see a neighbour, or it is not a watch tower
hardConstraints: a knoll with sight of the whole terrace system
preferences: a platform rather than a keep

occupants: D2 field-owners' men out of season

vibe.silhouette: A timber platform on four legs on the only knoll for kilometres, with a bell and a ladder that is taken away.
vibe.palette: Timber grey, saltrice silver in every direction, and one bright bell.
vibe.materials: Timber and reed; no stone, deliberately, so that it can be dismantled in a night.
vibe.signatureFeature: The removable ladder, which is where the politics live: whoever holds the ladder holds the tower.
vibe.condition: Simple, sound, rebuilt every few years.
vibe.approach: The platform is the only vertical in the terrace country and shows from every bank.
vibe.senses: Wind through standing crop; a bell; the ladder being carried away at dusk.

places.name: The Thorn Bond

why.founding: Saltrice going north and Dunmer goods coming south both need to sit somewhere lockable while the tolls are argued.
why.siteAdvantages: On Thorn's river quay, where cargo transfers between boat and the Tear road.
why.occupantsMotive: The bond is held by the field-owners jointly, which means it is held by nobody and audited by everybody.
why.pressures: Half the north's smuggling passes through it legitimately and leaves by a different door.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be seized by whichever faction won Thorn's title court outright.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: attached to a port or a wharf

occupants: one D3 who is not on the roll

vibe.silhouette: A long stone store on a quay with a great door at one end and a small one at the other that has no seal on it.
vibe.palette: Wet quay stone, black timber, red wax on one door only.
vibe.materials: Dres-built stone with an Argonian reed-roofed office bolted to the side.
vibe.signatureFeature: The second door: unsealed, unlisted, and worn smooth at the handle.
vibe.condition: Sound, well used, audited by nobody who wants to know.
vibe.approach: The great door faces the quay and the small one faces an alley, which is the whole story.
vibe.senses: Barrels; a tally called; a door that opens quietly at night.

why.founding: The north-east islands are flat, predator-free and surrounded by fishing water, so a colony has used them for as long as anyone knows.
why.siteAdvantages: A cluster of low islets in the delta, none big enough for a house and all of them white with birds.
why.occupantsMotive: The delta villages take eggs to a strict quota set by the oldest woman in each village and enforced absolutely.
why.pressures: Egging season and the fishing season overlap, and boats compete for the same water.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be stripped in three seasons if the quota ever lapsed, and every village says so about every other village.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: worked seasonally from a nearby settlement
preferences: a quota post on the nearest inhabited island

vibe.silhouette: Five low islets so covered in birds that the land looks like it is moving, with a cloud of them above.
vibe.palette: White on white on grey-green water, and the sky spotted with birds to a great height.
vibe.materials: Nothing built but one quota post on a stake in the water.
vibe.signatureFeature: The dusk lift: the whole colony rises at once and the sound arrives a second later.
vibe.condition: Unchanging.
vibe.approach: The noise carries three kilometres over water — the province's single strongest audible cue.
vibe.senses: A sound level that makes speech impossible; wings; ammonia.

places.name: The Tide Fair

why.founding: Delta villages, upland holdings and Dunmer caravans can all reach one hard sand bank at low spring tide and nowhere else together.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm sand flat exposed for six hours twice a month and under two metres of water the rest of the time.
why.occupantsMotive: Everyone trades because everyone can get here; nobody builds because in six hours the sea comes back.
why.pressures: The fair ends when the tide says so, which is the only rule and is absolutely enforced.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be impossible if the delta shifted, and the delta shifts.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: a landing, because most goods come by water
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on neutral ground between settlements, or in an M3+ settlement
hardConstraints: a sand flat exposed at spring low tide

notableNpcSlots: the tide-caller

vibe.silhouette: A hundred boats drawn up on wet sand around a market that exists for six hours and leaves no trace.
vibe.palette: Wet sand silver, boat hulls of a dozen colours, sky doubled in the sheet water.
vibe.materials: Nothing built at all. The market's entire fabric arrives by boat and leaves by boat.
vibe.signatureFeature: The tide marker, a single pole, and the horn blown when the water reaches its second band.
vibe.condition: Utterly impermanent — the most literal expression of the province's building ethic.
vibe.approach: You arrive by water onto ground that is only there today, which no other market in the province offers.
vibe.senses: A hundred hulls on sand; a horn; water beginning to run in the low channels.

places.name: The Two-Gate Bridge

why.founding: The Tear road crosses the north-eastern river once, and both banks belong to different interests.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock narrows with abutments on each side — the only single-span crossing on the river.
why.occupantsMotive: Each bank has built its own gate house, and a cart pays twice or argues twice.
why.pressures: The two toll-holders have not spoken directly in nine years and communicate by written notes carried across.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be one toll if either bank bought out the other, which both have refused on principle.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: spans a channel at its narrowest
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the route graph; its owner lives within sight
hardConstraints: a single-span narrows on the Tear road
preferences: a gate house at each end

occupants: D1 toll hands at each end

vibe.silhouette: One bridge with two gate houses, one at each end, painted in different colours and facing each other.
vibe.palette: River green below, and two gate houses in deliberately clashing paint.
vibe.materials: A Dres-built stone span with two Argonian timber gate houses added at opposite ends.
vibe.signatureFeature: The note line: a cord strung under the deck, with a box on it, for messages between people who will not meet.
vibe.condition: The bridge is sound and both gate houses are over-built.
vibe.approach: You see the first gate house and assume you have paid; then you cross and see the second.
vibe.senses: Two bells; the cord and box running under the deck; the river.

why.founding: A large Kothringi-Argonian village that the Flu emptied in one season and nobody has since reoccupied.
why.siteAdvantages: Good high ground on the channel network — so good that its emptiness is the most conspicuous thing in the district.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies it but the taboo, which is now maintained by habit rather than fear.
why.pressures: Boat crews use its landing and will not sleep above the landing steps, a line they observe without discussing.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be resettled tomorrow by anyone who did not grow up here.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in the country the Flu emptied; other villages avoid it

vibe.silhouette: Two hundred roof frames with no thatch on them, standing in rows on a rise, silhouetted like ribs.
vibe.palette: Bare grey timber, green ground, sky through every roof.
vibe.materials: Argonian frames without their reed — the impermanent material went and the frames stayed, which is backwards.
vibe.signatureFeature: The frames: reed rots in years, so a village with standing frames and no thatch has been empty for exactly the wrong length of time.
vibe.condition: Skeletal, stable, unlooted.
vibe.approach: From the channel the rise is a fence of vertical timbers against the sky, visible at eight hundred metres.
vibe.senses: Wind through two hundred empty frames, which makes a sound like a single low note.

places.name: The Veterans' Ridge

why.founding: Argonians who went north into Morrowind in 4E 5–6 and came back settled together on the ridge that looks at the pass they came home through.
why.siteAdvantages: High ground with a clear line to the pass, chosen for the view rather than the soil.
why.occupantsMotive: Their grandchildren hold it as an institution: a place where the invasion is remembered as a victory, in a province that mostly does not discuss it.
why.pressures: The Dres holding is four hours away and both households know exactly what the other is.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose its meaning entirely when the last person who was told the story by a participant dies.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: toward the Morrowind border and the Tear road
hardConstraints: a ridge with a line to the pass

notableNpcSlots: the hall-holder
the keeper of the taken banners

vibe.silhouette: A long low hall on a ridge with every house behind it facing north, and Dunmer banners nailed to the gable.
vibe.palette: Ridge brown, thatch, and the faded reds of captured Velothi cloth.
vibe.materials: Argonian construction throughout; every trophy in it is Dunmer.
vibe.signatureFeature: The gable banners: taken in 4E 6, rehung every year, deliberately fading rather than replaced.
vibe.condition: Well kept; the hall is the best-built Argonian building in the district.
vibe.approach: The hall's ridge line and the banners read against the sky from the road below.
vibe.senses: A drum in the evening; wind on the ridge; old men arguing about a date.

places.name: The Shrine of Haynekhtnamet
sources: uesp:Lore:Wamasu (Haynekhtnamet of Shadowfen received offerings to stop seasonal flooding)

why.founding: Canon names a wamasu of Shadowfen that received offerings to stop the seasonal flooding; the shrine is where they were left.
why.siteAdvantages: On the bank above the pond the creature is held to inhabit, at the highest point the flood reaches.
why.occupantsMotive: Four villages send offerings each wet season, in rotation, and none of them will say they believe it works.
why.pressures: The offerings are increasingly practical — tools and salt rather than symbols — which the older villagers find embarrassing.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned in a dry decade and re-established within a week of the next bad flood.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: between a village and a lair
hardConstraints: above a wamasu pond at flood height

vibe.silhouette: A stone shelf on a bank above black water, loaded with tools, salt and cord, all of it slowly corroding.
vibe.palette: Green-black water, corroded iron, salt white, and scorch marks on the shelf.
vibe.materials: One dressed stone shelf and nothing else; the province's minimum viable shrine.
vibe.signatureFeature: The scorch marks: the shelf is periodically struck, and the offerings nearest the water are always the most burnt.
vibe.condition: The shelf is ancient; everything on it is from this year or last.
vibe.approach: You smell ozone before you see the water, which is the only warning you get.
vibe.senses: Water; a crackle that is not a fire; hair standing up.

places.name: The Unpermitted Cut

why.founding: Somebody is digging on the far side of Outer Silyanorn without a permit, at night, for something specific.
why.siteAdvantages: Behind the ruin's spoil ridge, where the licensed dig's fence blocks the line of sight from the road.
why.occupantsMotive: The diggers are hired; the person paying them is not here and communicates by written instruction.
why.pressures: The instructions name a chamber that is not on any plan the Collections holds.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned within an hour of discovery, and the instructions burned.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor, or at an unwatched ruin
hardConstraints: out of sight of a licensed dig
preferences: a spoil ridge as a screen

occupants: one D3 overseer with the instructions

vibe.silhouette: A cut into the spoil ridge with hooded lamps in it, worked at night and covered with brush by day.
vibe.palette: Lamp light held down to a slot; spoil brown; brush green over everything.
vibe.materials: No structure whatsoever — hooded lamps, brush screens and a rope ladder into the cut.
vibe.signatureFeature: The instruction sheet, weighted with a stone at the cut's edge, in a hand nobody here can read.
vibe.condition: Concealed daily, worked nightly, three weeks old.
vibe.approach: By day it is a brush pile. The cue is at night and it is a light where no light should be.
vibe.senses: Digging kept deliberately quiet; a lamp hood being adjusted; nobody talking.

places.name: The White Pans

why.founding: Salt is the north's second currency — the Tear road stage prefers it to coin — and the delta makes it for free given sun and time.
why.siteAdvantages: A flat tidal margin with high evaporation and a rock bar that keeps the sea out except when wanted.
why.occupantsMotive: Six families work the pans in a rotation set by tide rather than by agreement, which prevents most quarrels.
why.pressures: The salt smugglers on the rim ledge buy here, and the pans do not ask.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would flood permanently if the rock bar were breached, and the north's barter economy would notice.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: tidal salt water, sun and wind
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: supplies a whole district's preservation
hardConstraints: a flat tidal margin behind a bar
preferences: a salt store above the tide

occupants: D2 at the bar in a high tide

vibe.silhouette: A grid of shallow pans in every stage from grey water to blinding white, with rakes standing in the finished ones.
vibe.palette: White, grey, and a pink stain in two pans that nobody has explained.
vibe.materials: Clay pan walls and timber rakes; the store is reed on a stone plinth.
vibe.signatureFeature: The pink pans: two of the grid go rose-coloured every summer and are worked last, for luck.
vibe.condition: Rebuilt each season; the pan walls are re-puddled every spring.
vibe.approach: The white reads from a kilometre in sunlight — the brightest thing in the province.
vibe.senses: Rakes on crust; gulls; wind carrying salt into your mouth.

places.name: The Xanmeer Hold
sources: uesp:Lore:Xanmeer (some tribes live in them for their walls and working defences)

why.founding: A tribe took a xanmeer's walls and working ancient defences and has lived in them ever since — the strongest fortification in the north.
why.siteAdvantages: A terraced stone mass on firm ground in the channels, with the ancient mechanisms still functional on the lower terraces.
why.occupantsMotive: They live here because the north has been raided by Sul-Xan, Naga and Umbriel within four centuries and the walls have held each time.
why.pressures: Living in stone is a compromise their neighbours notice; their answer is that they did not build it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the north's refuge of last resort in any real emergency, and the tribe has said as much.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: dominates its immediate district
hardConstraints: a standing xanmeer with working defences

notableNpcSlots: the hold-holder
the mechanism-keeper who does not know how it works

vibe.silhouette: A stepped stone mass with reed houses built on every terrace, smoke from all of them, and a barred stone gate at the bottom.
vibe.palette: Grey stone in terraces, reed gold in horizontal bands, smoke.
vibe.materials: Ancient xanmeer stone with an entirely modern Argonian village built onto it in reed and mud, unbonded and reversible.
vibe.signatureFeature: The living terraces: houses that could be taken down in a day standing on stone that has stood four thousand years.
vibe.condition: The stone is maintained where it defends and ignored where it does not; the reed is rebuilt on the usual cycle.
vibe.approach: The stepped silhouette with smoke rising from every level reads over the canopy at a kilometre — the north's most legible landmark.
vibe.senses: A great many households at close quarters; the gate mechanism, which is the loudest sound in the district.

places.name: Thorn

why.founding: The one city with real fields around it: saltrice on temperate grassland, grown first for House Dres and now for whoever holds the title.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm grassland above a delta, with the Tear road out to Morrowind and river access down to the coast — the only place in Argonia where all three meet.
why.occupantsMotive: The vicecanon governs; the field-owners actually decide; the Dunmer minority holds the trade and remembers who used to hold the people.
why.pressures: Every field title is disputed, the guards look away from the smuggling because the smuggling pays them, and the border tolls fund both sides of the argument.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would tear itself apart if Morrowind ever pressed a claim, and knows it.

vibe.silhouette: A low walled city sitting in a sea of pale saltrice, with one grey Hist crown outside the wall and nothing inside taller than it.
vibe.palette: Saltrice silver-green, wall dun, Dunmer-quarter red lacquer, and the Hist's pale grey.
vibe.materials: Argonian mud and reed inside the wall; Velothi-influenced timber and lacquer in the Dunmer quarter; the two never blend.
vibe.signatureFeature: The Hist outside the walls — a tree the city depends on and deliberately did not enclose.
vibe.condition: Prosperous, over-guarded at the gates and under-guarded everywhere else.
vibe.mood: Wealthy, litigious, morally compromised, and entirely aware of it.
vibe.approach: Across the fields you see the wall as a low line and the Hist crown above it long before you see a roof.
vibe.senses: Wind through standing saltrice; a Dunmer market bell; guar caravans; the wet-season frogs in the delta.

places.complexityJustification: A major city with a walled core, an unblended Dunmer trade quarter, an outside-the-walls Hist and a working field system that must be compiled as landscape as well as settlement.

places.name: The Thorn Terraces

why.founding: Saltrice is the north's cash crop and the only reason a foreign house ever wanted this ground; the terraces are what four centuries of that wanting built.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow tilt of grassland above the delta, where salt water can be admitted in controlled amounts — saltrice needs both.
why.occupantsMotive: The terraces are worked by the villages and owned, on paper, by whoever last won in Thorn's title court.
why.pressures: The salt gates are the whole system, and three of the eleven are held by a single family who charge for them.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would fail as a crop within two seasons if the salt gates were ever lost to a delta shift.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in a city's hinterland; owned
hardConstraints: a tilt of ground above brackish water

notableNpcSlots: the family who hold three gates

vibe.silhouette: Eleven wide terraces of standing water stepping down to a delta, each a different shade, with a stone gate at the head of every bank.
vibe.palette: Saltrice silver-green, brackish grey water, salt crust white at the gate lips.
vibe.materials: Earth bunds with cut stone gates; the gates are the only masonry and they are Dres-built.
vibe.signatureFeature: The salt crust: every gate has a white rime that tells you exactly how it is being worked.
vibe.condition: Bunds immaculate, gates ancient and increasingly patched.
vibe.approach: From the Tear road the terraces flash in sequence as you descend — the largest visual event in the north.
vibe.senses: Water through gates; bird-scarers; a great deal of standing water in wind.

places.name: The Rat Gallery
sources: world/sources/lore/topics/prisons.md (Warden Varus's Tunnel Rats digging for crystals)

why.founding: An Imperial warden once worked penal labour into these galleries for crystal, promising limited freedom; the gallery outlived the warden, the promise and the Empire.
why.siteAdvantages: The deepest reachable level of the undercity, below the licensed diggings, where the seams the diggers will not risk still run.
why.occupantsMotive: The people down here are working an Owing that has been transferred so many times nobody can name the original creditor.
why.pressures: The gallery floods on a schedule nobody controls, and the licensed diggers above have stopped pretending they don't know.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty in a day if the Owing ledgers above it were voided — which is the whole hook.

vibe.silhouette: A single hoist shaft going down into the dark, and below it galleries you cannot stand up in.
vibe.palette: Black, lamp yellow, wet Ayleid white where a lamp catches carving.
vibe.materials: Ayleid galleries reduced to crawl-ways by spoil; timber props; nothing built, only narrowed.
vibe.signatureFeature: The flood tally scratched by the hoist: days since, and days between, kept by the people down there.
vibe.condition: Structurally appalling; it works because nobody above has to look at it.
vibe.approach: There is no cue at all above ground but the hoist frame, which looks like the diggings' equipment.
vibe.senses: Water moving somewhere below; a hoist rope; breathing in a confined space.

why.founding: A Kothringi settlement that died in 2E 561, one year into the Flu, with its founder's name still on it.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm bank on the Shadowfen channels — good ground, which is why nobody has taken it and everyone can see it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; the neighbouring villages route boats past it without stopping, and have for three hundred years.
why.pressures: It is the best unclaimed landing in the district, and the taboo is the only thing keeping it unclaimed.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be resettled within a decade if the north ever grew enough to need the ground.

vibe.silhouette: A stone landing with a name cut into it, and behind it a settlement whose walls stand and whose roofs do not.
vibe.palette: Silver-grey stone, black doorways, and a green that has grown to the doorsteps and stopped.
vibe.materials: Kothringi coursed stone, finer than anything around it; not one Argonian repair anywhere.
vibe.signatureFeature: The name at the landing — the founder's, still legible, still uneffaced.
vibe.condition: Untouched. Nothing has been taken, which after three centuries is remarkable.
vibe.approach: From the channel you see the landing steps first and the name is at eye height from a boat.
vibe.senses: Water on stone steps; wind through roofless rooms; no boats stopping.
